result.track: M: measurement (real-network numbers for round 2; cached data, CPU, 4 threads)
result.summary: On ResNet-18 and ResNet-50, six measurements kill four candidates: E6's test on the always-on read misses by 2e6 to 2e9, the C10 LP reaches at most 1e-7 of the table's fit, nu is at least .17 so C4 is dead at k = 14, and Test Q misses family patches by 1e11 to 1e19 at the median. They also measure the common block: at k = 14 only .12 of the table's loss is conditional inside a row's own family of about 28 classes (D2's minors reach .007), .70 is conditional inside stranger families, and .18 is mass between families. The loss has two tail regimes, not one: e < -1 holds .46 to .60 (linear), and e > 1 holds .29 to .34 (exponential), so "L1 or tropical" describes only the down side; measurements fill no slot.

The least eigenvalue over classes is (C-1)/C times eta_up. Its direction reads the class at a weighted mean probability equal to eta_up within a factor of 1.1 to 1.7 (2.06e-7 at R18 k = 14), while that class's mean probability is 1.1e-3. The least q in the table is 7e-37 to 4e-22.
statements.proof: Estimator, written in m4_e6.py before the run. zeta = (1, whitened standardised z), so sum p zeta zeta^T = I. Gamma_0 = sum p (s - q) zeta^T; Gamma = its non-Y columns. g_perp = |(I - QQ^T) Gamma (I - P_M0)|_op. Gauge: V - mean = Q R, M_0 = R (Z M)^T zhat / n, sigma = least singular value of M_0. A_i = sum p q_x[i](1 - q_x[i]) zeta zeta^T; eta_up = (C/(C-1)) min over i of lambda_min(A_i), an upper bound on eta by the test vector (e_i - 1/C) w^T. T1 = 2 sqrt(k*) g zeta_max / eta_up, T2 = 2 g / (eta_up sigma). Since eta_up >= eta, ratio >= 1 kills the test at this fit. The 3 smallest classes were rechecked with singular values of sqrt(p w) zeta. Floor: eta <= 1/(C-1) and zeta_max >= sqrt D (E6-reach check) give T1 >= 2 sqrt(k) g sqrt(D) (C-1). ResNet-50 uses about 200 screened classes, so its eta_up is still an upper bound; on ResNet-18 all 1000 were solved.
statements.covers: Always-on read (L_on) only. Not free codes, not the gated box. 20000 validation crops, not N's training P.
statements.check: Reproduced kl from the saved fits: 1.0618, .2360, .0207; .5282, .0850, .0074. The eigen recheck agrees with svd to 10 digits. Screen: on ResNet-18 the kth-weight score ranked the true least class 3rd, 2nd, 1st (Spearman .94, .95, .91). Control m0: eta true 2.04e-2, eta_up 2.17e-2 on a small read. Stationarity defects are not 0, so E6 does not literally apply and this measures distance from its test: |V^T Gamma|/|Gamma| = .005, .020, .098; .013, .048, .233; |Gamma M_0^T|/|Gamma| = .004, .014, .123; .005, .030, .160. Written prediction: ratio 1e5 to 1e9: hit. eta_up 1e-10 to 1e-6: hit. eta_up falling with k: FALSE (flat on R18, rising on R50). g near 1e-4: missed by a factor of 97; this is a normalisation: g here = sqrt(n) times pc_real_cert's number (.00968 / sqrt(20000) = 6.85e-5 against 6.88e-5, which came from a different fit). Kills E6's operator-norm test as a certificate on real reads, independently of eta. Supports referee E's corrected form: the read does steer onto rows where a class is at 2e-7. Against TQ18's 1e30 to 1e49 at k = 14, 38 the gain is about 22 to 40 orders, but the test stays dead. A sharper form must replace the operator norm, and this does not test the true ratio that track E named.

| R18 label, 14 | .2452 | 2.19e-9 | 0 | 2.20e-9 | 9.0e-9 |

Mechanism 1: at the double-centred (a, g), G_S <= 0 at every tree node. The margin m'(n/sqrt k'' - sqrt k'')/|A|_(r) has a maximum of .65 and .36 (R18, k = 14, 38) and .81 and .48 (R50). Only after an (a, g) search do 3 and 9 of the k = 14 columns on the label table go positive, and 8 on the top-class table.
Mechanism 2: transversal blocks (one class per family, disjoint) reach margin 1.05 on R50 at k = 14, but their least entry is about 1e-9, so their value is at most 5e-11. Peeled blocks at default (a, g) gave 0.
statements.proof:
Estimator, in m2_pack.py before the full run. Blocks = Ward nodes with n > r = k + 1, pairs (c, c). G_S and G'_S as in C10 and referee C's complement; grid b in {.25, .5, 1}, x0 in {.003, .03, .1, .3}. Nesting gives one constraint per tree node (the least s over pairs with that LCA) and one per class. Solution shrunk to exact feasibility; any (a, g) is valid, so a subgradient search on nodes up to 300 classes can only raise the value.
Mixed-LP lemma, proved here. Give each column S a share on each pair: w_S = xi_S/b off the diagonal and xi_S/x0 on it for a C10 column; xi_S/2 and xi_S for a complement column. Premise: the shares on each pair sum to at most p s. Let R = sum R^S. The map (w, y) -> w phi(y/w) is the perspective of a convex function, so it is jointly convex and homogeneous, hence subadditive, and the leftover share costs 0. So p s phi(-R/(p s)) <= sum over S of w_S phi(-R^S/w_S). Each argument is in [-b, b] off the diagonal for C10 (|T| <= 1), in [-1, 1] for the complement (|Pi_jl| <= 1/2), and in [-1, 0] on the diagonal. Each column's cost bound in its own proof then holds unchanged. Row sums and orthogonality hold column by column. So L_free(k) >= the sum of xi_S G over columns. QED.
statements.covers: The bound is a floor on L_free, so also L_table, L_on, V_b. Measured on two class-row tables.
statements.check: Control m0: on the level table K = 64, k = 14 the LP equals C11's formula to 5 digits and reaches .27, .31, .30 of a fit at e = .3, .1, .01. This reproduces round 1's 30%. Written prediction: under 1% of the fit: hit by far more. First prediction also said blocks would lose only to caps: wrong; the smoke showed G_S <= 0, so a second prediction was written after the smoke and before the full run: below 1%, transversal margin near or above 1, value under 1e-6 of the fit's scale: hit. Kills C10 and the complement as useful bounds on real tables at these blocks; coupling their blocks is not worth doing in this form, since each block is already near 0. It does not exclude other duals or block lists not tried. The 30% on level tails does not transfer: real tails have spread inside blocks.

statements.proof: Estimator, in m3_testq.py before the run. D3's premises (G_b doubly centred, orthogonal to L_b, patches summing to G) do not hold at a real fit, so G_b = the projection of the block of G onto those conditions, the best case for the patch. The block's norm kept: median .37 to .63 on R18, .35 to .61 on R50 at k = 14, 38. Share w = p q. Gt = G_b D_eta^(-1/2), Lt = (L_b - (L_b eta) 1^T) D_eta^(1/2), ct = Lt Ut. kappa^2 = |D_r^(-1/2) Gt|_op^2, lam_b = least eigenvalue of sum r_x (ct_x - cbar)(ct_x - cbar)^T. Necessary by corrected D6: kappa^2 / lam_b <= 1/4 at any B. Row condition: |Gt_x| <= rt_x. Ratio = max(4 kappa^2 / lam_b, max over x of |Gt_x|^2 / rt_x^2); 1 is the edge. A failure kills; a pass would not certify. D6 cap: certified loss <= sum over b, x of w[x, i*], i* = argmin w[x, i]/eta_i; it needs no residual.
statements.covers: Free codes and the table, for these patches and these eta only. Test F and other patch families were not measured.
statements.check: Control m0: on referee D's instance the code gives ratio_op .941, matching his w = .472 lam, and it scales as mu^2 (3.76, 15.05). My first control run used rho = q min; the right rho is p q min, and with it the control passes. The rank cap sum (|H| - 1 - k) lam / 4 is 9e-7 to 5e-4 of the fit. Prediction: median above 1, 1e3 to 1e8: above 1 hit, range FALSE (far larger). k = 38 a little better: FALSE (not better on R18). D6 cap more than 100 times below the loss at k = 14: hit. Family blocks hold under 20% of |G|^2: FALSE (.67, .51 on R18 k = 14, sizes 28, 16; .24 to .75 across rows). Kills Test Q at family patches: it cannot certify more than .75% of the loss at k = 14 with these patches and eta, whatever the residual. D2 and D3 keep only their letter on real tables.

result.blocked_by: Nothing blocks the six measurements. They fill no slot, and they do not give a dual that charges for sharing. The step still open for other tracks is this: no certificate here charges the stranger-family conditional, which holds .70 of the loss at k = 14. Every form tested fails first on that part or on tiny caps.

What other tracks should use.

result.summary: I identified the object at confidence: for k new top units, the least KL is e times (m + 1) V(mu, k) minus a tail entropy, up to a term with no tail depth in it, where V is a one-sided (walled) low-rank program over N's tail shape mu = s / e, and this holds for free codes and any always-on read, with only the upper side for the gated box. Each row's non-top classes must sit at least m below the top, a build pays mu times its overshoot, and A's log-q cancellation is now a dual point that depends on the competitor and works for any C and k. I found closed values of V at k = 1 (any weights), k = K - 2 and K = 2k, including tree tails where family minors read 0, but no closed value and no matching bound at k < K/2, and no slot is filled because this is a limit-type result with no claim errors.

statements.statement: H1 (the wall theorem: an inequality at every confidence, with no tail depth in it). Rows x have weights p_x > 0, sum 1, and a top class tau(x). Fix e with e >= the tail mass of every row, m = log(1/e). Write s_x[i] = e mu_xi for i != tau(x), mu_xi >= 0, and s_x[tau(x)] = 1 - e w_x with w_x = sum_i mu_xi <= 1. h_x = -sum_i mu_xi log mu_xi >= 0. hbar = sum p h, wbar = sum p w, p_min = least p_x. Let l_x = A Y[x] + V c_x be a logit class, with c in a linear code class Z (free codes: Z = R^n; always-on read: Z = span of Y and z). Let M_xi = l_x[tau(x)] - l_x[i]. Define V = V_Z(mu, k) = inf of sum over x, i != tau(x) of p_x mu_xi (M_xi - 1) over the class, subject to M_xi >= 1 for ALL x and i != tau(x) (V = +inf if nothing is feasible). Let Lam = V + wbar. Then (a) Upper, if V < inf: L_Z(k) / e <= (m + 1) V - hbar + Lam log_+((C - 1)/Lam) + e. (b) Lower, for every v0 in [0, V] with e (v0 + wbar) <= p_min, and with Lam0 = v0 + wbar: L_Z(k) / e >= (m + 1) v0 - hbar - Lam0 log_+(Lam0 / p_min) - e Lam0^2 / p_min. (c) (a) holds also for V_b(k) with V^b, the same program over gated units, since it only needs a logit class closed under positive scaling; then V_free <= V^b, and V_b(k) >= L_free(k) gives (b) with V_free. No least tail entry, no eta, no rho, and no block appears. Entries with mu_xi = 0 are allowed. Rows may be photos or regions.
statements.proof: Upper. Take a near-optimal feasible logit table, and let delta = log_+((C-1)/Lam), m' = m + delta. Scale it by m' (the class is a linear space, or closed under scaling) and gauge the top logit to 0, so d_i = -m' M_i. With a = 1 - e w, Z = 1 + sum exp(d_i), the exact identity is KL(s_x || softmax) = a log a + log Z + sum_i e mu_i (-m + log mu_i + m' M_i). Then log Z <= Z - 1 <= (C-1) e exp(-delta), because M_i >= 1. Also a log a <= -e w + e^2 w^2, since (1-u)log(1-u) = -u + sum_{j>=2} u^j/(j(j-1)) and sum 1/(j(j-1)) = 1. Summing with p and using sum p mu M = V + wbar gives L/e <= m V + delta Lam - hbar - wbar + (C-1) exp(-delta) + e. If Lam < C-1 then (C-1)exp(-delta) = Lam and the right side is (m+1)V + Lam log((C-1)/Lam) - hbar + e. If Lam >= C-1 then delta = 0 and C-1 <= Lam gives the same form with log_+ = 0. Lower. Fix V (the matrix). For fixed V, M is linear in w = (A, c), and LP(V) = min sum p mu (M(w) - 1) s.t. M(w) >= 1 has dual max { sum (y - p mu) : y >= 0 on tail entries, <y - p mu, M(w)> = 0 for all w }. Its value is 0 at y = p mu. If the primal is feasible, strong duality gives value Val_V >= V >= v0. If it is infeasible, the dual is unbounded. In both cases a convex combination (or a point on the ray) gives a dual feasible y with sum (y - p mu) = v0 exactly, so sum y = Lam0. Set R_xi = y_xi - p_x mu_xi on the tail and R_x,tau = -sum_tail R_xi. Then <R, l> = -<y - p mu, M> = 0 for every logit in the class. Let q°_xi = e y_xi / p_x on the tail, q°_tau = 1 - e y_x / p_x with y_x = sum_i y_xi; this is a distribution, since e Lam0 <= p_min. For every l in the class, the Gibbs variational bound log sum e^l >= <q°, l> + H(q°) gives sum p KL(s || softmax l) >= sum p [H(q°_x) - H(s_x)] + e <R, l> = sum p [H(q°_x) - H(s_x)]. Now compute. H(s_x) = -a log a + e m w_x + e h_x. H(q°_x) = -q°_tau log q°_tau + (e/p_x) sum y_xi (m + log(p_x / y_xi)). So the difference summed with p is e m v0 + e sum y log(p/y) - e hbar + sum p [a log a - q°_tau log q°_tau]. Here log mu has cancelled: the cost q° log(q°/s) and the gain q° (log s) meet, which is A's cancellation in general form. Then y_xi <= Lam0 gives sum y log(p/y) >= -Lam0 log_+(Lam0/p_min). Also a log a >= -e w (from log a >= -(1-a)/a), and -q log q >= q(1-q) gives p_x q°_tau (1 - q°_tau) >= e y_x - e^2 y_x^2 / p_x. Summing: sum p [..] >= e (Lam0 - wbar) - e^2 Lam0^2 / p_min = e v0 - e^2 Lam0^2 / p_min. This holds at every V, so it holds at the infimum. QED.

Also, H2 is not a limit in a fixed exponent table: if s_x[i] proportional to exp(-m A_xi) with several exponents, then only tail entries of the largest scale keep weight, so mu has zeros, and walls stay at M >= 1 for all entries. If V = 0 on such a mu, then L is o(e m) and the piecewise-linear value says nothing further.

statements.statement: H3 (the structure of the program, rows = classes, K = C, tau(c) = c). Let n_ci = p_c mu_ci, and let l_c[i] = t_i + v_i . c_c. (1) M_ci + M_ic = S_ci = <v_c - v_i, c_c - c_i>, with no t in it. (2) M >= 1 is feasible for (V, c) with some t iff for every cycle (i_1, ..., i_l), the sum over j of <c_(i_j), v_(i_j) - v_(i_(j+1))> >= l. This is cyclic monotonicity with a margin: the codes sit in the cells of a power diagram of F(x) = max_i (t_i + v_i . x). (3) If n is balanced (sum_i n_ci = sum_i n_ic for each c), the objective has no t, and it is a sum of cycle sums. Under Fact F8 with label regions and uniform p, n is balanced: Fact F8 says the mean softmax equals the label share, and that is the same statement. (4) In the level case, f := sum_(c != i) (M_ci - 1) = K tr(Vbar^T Cbar) - K(K-1), with Vbar, Cbar centred. (5) Let Abar_ci = (M_ci + M_ic)/2 - 1 >= 0 for c != i, with diagonal 0, and A_ci = M_ci - 1. For x with sum x = 0: x^T Abar x - |x|^2 = -<V^T x, C^T x>. So on W_V = {x perp 1, V^T x = 0}, of dimension >= d := K - 1 - k, x^T Abar x = |x|^2 exactly. (6) So for a projector Pi onto a d-dimensional subspace of W_V: sum_(c != i) Pi_ci Abar_ci = d. (7) The program is linear for fixed V, and bilinear overall. It is classical rank in L and tropical only in the softmax (the top-class max); it is not a tropical rank problem.
statements.proof: (1) Expand: t and the row constants cancel. (2) t_c - t_i >= 1 - (v_c - v_i) . c_c are difference constraints, and Bellman-Ford feasibility holds iff no cycle is negative. M_ci > 0 for all i is the cell condition. (3) sum n_ci (t_c - t_i) = sum t_c (sum_i n_ci - sum_i n_ic). Flow decomposition gives the cycles. Fact F8: sum_c p_c s_c[i] = p_i gives sum_(c != i) p_c s_c[i] = p_i (1 - s_i[i]) = sum_(j != i) p_i s_i[j]. (4) sum_(c<i) <v_c - v_i, c_c - c_i> = K sum <vbar_c, cbar_c>. (5) sum_(c,i) x_c x_i S_ci = 2 (sum x)(sum x_c <v_c, c_c>) - 2 <V^T x, C^T x> = -2 <V^T x, C^T x>. Also S = 2(11^T - I) + 2 Abar gives sum x_c x_i S_ci = -2 |x|^2 + 2 x^T Abar x. (6) Trace. (7) M is linear in (t, c) at fixed V. QED.

statements.statement: H4 (k = 1, any K, any weights: exact, and this is not a linear program over order types). Rows = classes. V(n, 1) = the least over orders of the classes and over gaps u_j > 0 of sum_(c<i) { n_ci [ (i-c-1) + 2 sum_(j=c)^(i-1) (x_j - x_c)/u_j ] + n_ic [ (i-c-1) + 2 sum_(j=c)^(i-1) (x_i - x_(j+1))/u_j ] }, where x_j is the partial sum of the u. For each order this is a geometric program. (a) Level table: u uniform is optimal, M_ci = (c-i)^2, V = c(K, 1) = (K+3)(K-2)/6, that is L_free(1) / (e m) -> (K+3)(K-2)/6. (b) K = 3: V = the least over the middle class b, with ends a, c, of n_ac + n_ca + 4 sqrt(n_ac n_ca). (c) So on a table with rational entries the limit value can be irrational: mu rows (0, .8, .2), (.5, 0, .5), (.6, .4, 0), p = 1/3, gives V = 4/15 + 4/sqrt(75). So the limit is not the value of any finite union of linear programs with rational coefficients indexed by sign patterns or order types.
statements.proof: With k = 1, M >= 1 forces the codes into the K distinct cells of a convex piecewise-linear F. So all slopes differ, and classes sorted by slope have x_1 < ... < x_K. Let delta_j = v_(j+1) - v_j, b_j the crossing of lines j, j+1. Let alpha_j = M_(j,j+1) = delta_j (b_j - x_j) >= 1, and gamma_j = M_(j+1,j) = delta_j (x_(j+1) - b_j) >= 1, so delta_j u_j = alpha_j + gamma_j. Telescoping lines: for c < i, M_ci = sum_(j=c)^(i-1) delta_j (b_j - x_c) = sum [alpha_j + (alpha_j + gamma_j)(x_j - x_c)/u_j], and M_ic = sum [gamma_j + (alpha_j + gamma_j)(x_i - x_(j+1))/u_j]. Every (u > 0, alpha, gamma >= 1) is realised by some t, v, x, and all M_ci are >= i - c >= 1 then. The objective increases in alpha and gamma, so alpha = gamma = 1. That is the formula. (a) M_ci + M_ic = 2 (sum u_j)(sum 1/u_j) >= 2 (i-c)^2 by Cauchy, with equality at uniform u. Sum: f = K(K-1)(K+3)(K-2)/6, and c = f/(K(K-1)). (b) K = 3: overshoot n_ac (1 + 2 r) + n_ca (1 + 2/r) with r = u_1/u_2, and the neighbours overshoot 0. Minimise over r. (c) The three values for the given table are .8963, .7285, 1.2766. The least is at middle class 2, with n_13 = 1/15, n_31 = 1/5. A rational LP has a rational value. QED.

Let c(K, k) = lim L_table(k) / (e m) = V, f(K, k) = K (K-1) c(K, k) = the least of sum_(c != i) (M_ci - 1), and d = K - 1 - k. (1) For 1 <= k <= K-2: f(K, k) >= 2 K d / (K - 2) (projector), and f(K, k) >= K d / (k + 1) (the limit of C11; not re-derived). (2) f(K, k-) is nondecreasing as k falls, and c(K, k) is nondecreasing in K. (3) Exact: c(K, K-1) = 0; c(K, K-2) = 2 / ((K-1)(K-2)), that is f = 2K/(K-2), attained by M = 1 except M_12 = M_21 = 2 (K-1)/(K-2); c(2k, k) = 1/(2k - 1), that is f = K, attained by a pairing with M = 2 on partners; c(K, 1) = (K+3)(K-2)/6. (4) CORRECTION to the brief: c(K, k) does not tend to 1 at K = 2k. c(64, 32) = 1/63. What tends to 1 at K = 2k is the ratio of the projector bound to the true value, and L / (beta m) with beta = e/(K-1), which is what the referee's '.990' measured. (5) Upper bounds that are not closed forms: Petersen gives c(10, 4) <= 1/3, Clebsch gives c(16, 5) <= 1/3 (f = 30 and 80), triangular-lattice patches give f(7, 2) <= 42. Measured upper bounds: c(64, 14) <= .2423 by my own run, c(64, 7) <= .788, with the round 1 fit slopes .217 and .72 being lower, so my runs are not converged.

Then |Pi(e_c + e_i)|^2 <= 2 - 4/K, and Pi_ci = (|Pi(e_c + e_i)|^2 - |Pi(e_c - e_i)|^2)/4 <= 1/2 - 1/K. Since Abar >= 0: d = sum Pi_ci Abar_ci <= (1/2 - 1/K) f. (2) A principal submatrix of M is feasible for the same k. Averaging over subsets of size K - 1, each ordered pair lies in K - 2 of them: (K-2) f(K,k) >= K f(K-1,k). (3) k = K-2: x = (K-2, K-2, -2, ..., -2) has M x = 2 * 1 for the stated M: row j >= 3 gives -x_j = 2; row 1 gives (K-2)(M_12 - 2) = 2. So rank J M J <= K-2, and any zero-diagonal M with that rank is t + V c up to row constants. Then f = 2 (M_12 - 1) = 2K/(K-2), which equals the bound (1). k = K/2: J M J = -J(I - P)J has rank K/2 with P the pairing, f = K, equal to (1) at d = K/2 - 1. k = 1 is H4. (4) From (3). (5) Direct: Petersen adjacency A has eigenvalues 3, 1^5, -2^4, and M = 11^T - I + A has rank J M J = 4, and it is an EDM; Clebsch 5, 1^10, -3^5 likewise. QED.

statements.statement: H6 (tree and attribute tails: the value, and a charge for sharing). Rows = classes. Let nmin = the least n_ci. (1) For any tail: V(n, k) >= nmin f(K, k), with equality exactly when some level-optimal M has overshoot only on entries of value nmin. (2) If the entries with value nmin hold a perfect matching, then V(n, K/2) = K nmin; if they hold a pair with n_ci = n_ic = nmin, then V(n, K-2) = (2K/(K-2)) nmin. (3) Tree tail: K = 2^h, p uniform, mu by common-ancestor level, with far mass t split evenly on the K/2 far classes, mu_far = 2 t / K. Then V(n, K/2) = mu_far and, by H1, L_free(K/2)/e = (m+1) mu_far - hbar + O(Lam log(K^2)). The partner of each class is a FAR cousin; relatives sit at the margin M = 1. This least has top class up to 1 - e and a real relative order in the tail. (4) Charge for sharing with no competitor and no block: K = J f classes, family size f, each row's far share t spread evenly on (J-1) f classes, near entries at least as large. At k = f - 1 every family minor of TQ22 reads 0, yet V >= t / (k + 1). So L_free(k) >= e [ m t / (k+1) ](1 - o(1)), and this loss is all between families. (5) Kept-attribute builds: on 2^h classes in a product tail, a build with k < h independent attributes has M = 0 on a pair, so it is outside the wall and pays a constant, not e m. At k = h the Hamming build has V = sum_j mu(j)(j-1), and it is not the least on most shapes tested.
statements.proof: (1) Monotone in n, with Abar >= 0: sum n_ci A_ci >= nmin sum A_ci. Equality needs the support condition. (2) Upper: the builds of H5 (3) with the overshoot on those entries. Lower: (1) with H5. (3) The far graph of a perfect binary tree is complete bipartite, so it has a perfect matching. nmin = mu_far / K. (4) Lower bound (1) with f >= K d / (k+1), d = (J-1) f, nmin = t / ((J-1) f K). (5) M_ci = 0 violates the wall. By H1's lower side with V = +inf for that class, or directly, the row loses order 1 once top tie is forced. QED.

statements.statement: H7 (B's missing statement, as written, is the wrong statement). The statement 'for every rank-k L, the sum of n_xi |L_xi - a_x - T_xi| is at least a number from T' cannot carry the least. For every table with tail mass e and k >= 0, L = 0, a = 0 gives sum n |L - a - T| <= e (m w + hbar + 1) on the tail, with small top cost. While L_free(k) / e is about (m+1) V, and V = (K+3)(K-2)/6 at k = 1 on the level table. So plain two-sided weighted L1 has ratio to the true least tending to 0 by a factor of order K^2. The correct form is one-sided, with the wall: for every rank-k L with L_xi - L_x,tau <= -m on all tail entries, sum n (T - L) has least about e m V. A finite slope (pinball) version of the wall works only with slope B about (V + 1)/(p mu) on violated entries.
statements.proof: Direct computation of the two-sided cost at L = 0. By B1, KL = min over a of sum n psi(l - a - T), and psi(y) grows exponentially for y > 0 and linearly for y < 0. Its scaled limit (1/m) psi(m y) is (-y)_+ plus a wall at y > 0, by epi-convergence. So the wall is not a detail. On the tail, the entries above the wall carry q mass, not n times distance. The slope estimate: scaling a violating M by 1/(1 - delta) restores the wall at cost delta (V + 1), so slope (V+1)/(p mu) on the violated entry is an exact penalty.

statements.statement: H8 (cubic bound, only under two named premises). Suppose a build is Euclid (V = C after an invertible change of basis, so M_ci = |x_c - x_i|^2 / 2 with x in R^k) and Abar has equal row sums rho, with d >= k / sqrt 3. Then rho^3 + d >= (rho + d)^3 / k^2, so rho >= rho*(K, k), the root. Equality holds at triangle-free regular structures: rho* = 3 at (10, 4), Petersen; 5 at (16, 5), Clebsch; 5 at (56, 20), Gewirtz with scale 1/2; 8 at (77, 21), M22 with scale 1/2. At (64, 14), rho* = 9.995, that is c >= .159 inside this class, against .052 proved in general and <= .217 measured. The premise of equal row sums cannot be dropped: at (5, 2), rho* = 3.236 (pentagon), while an irregular patch of the triangular lattice has f = 14, C = 2.8.
statements.proof: By H3 (5) with Y = x x^T centred: I - Abar = Y on 1 perp, positive semidefinite of rank <= k. So on 1 perp, Abar has eigenvalue 1 with multiplicity >= d and others nu_1, ..., nu_k <= 1. The vector 1 has eigenvalue rho. tr Abar = 0 gives sum nu = -S, S = rho + d. tr Abar^3 >= 0, since Abar >= 0 entrywise, gives rho^3 + d + sum nu^3 >= 0. Let pi = the sum of positive nu, and j their count. Since nu^3 <= nu on [0, 1], and the negatives have count <= k - j and sum S + pi in absolute value: sum nu^3 <= pi - (S + pi)^3 / (k-j)^2 <= pi - S^3 / k^2 - 3 S^2 pi / k^2 <= -S^3 / k^2, when S >= k / sqrt 3. QED. Equality needs nu all equal and no triangle in the support. At (5,2) the five-point patch has M = 1, 1, 1, 3, 4 type entries.

statements.statement: H9 (Euclid). For every K and k, on the level table and on symmetric n: the least of the program is attained by V = C, so c(K, k) is a minimum-energy packing constant: K points in R^k, all squared distances >= 2, least mean squared distance. On centred points on a sphere this is exactly the Tammes problem, since then C + K - 1 = K / (1 - rho) with rho the largest inner product. So I do not expect a closed form for c(K, k) at general K, k; this is an expectation and not a theorem. Route: k = 1 is proved through increments x_(j+1) - x_j = sqrt(u_j delta_j) and Cauchy, which give (x_i - x_c)^2 <= S_ci. For general k, find x in R^k with 2 <= |x_c - x_i|^2 <= S_ci.
statements.proof: Not proved. For k >= 2 the positive part of the symmetric part of V C^T gives a feasible Euclid build, but its trace rises by the negative part. The k = 1 geometric mean has no proved analogue, and it must use the longer cycles of H3 (2), not only the 2-cycles.

statements.statement: Lemma G1 (overflow: Sylvester's inequality with numbers). Let Lh be a real matrix of rank <= k, with rows and columns split into J blocks; Ah_b are the diagonal blocks and Off = Lh minus those blocks. (a) For theta > 0 let r_b = the number of singular values of Ah_b above theta and o = sum r_b - k. If o >= 1 then sigma_j(Off) > theta for j = 1..o, so the Ky Fan norm |Off|_(o) >= o theta. (b) For J = 2, write Lh = [A B; C D], r_1 = the number of singular values of A above theta_1, r_2 the same for D at theta_2, o = r_1 + r_2 - k >= 1. Then sigma_i(C) sigma_(o+1-i)(B) > theta_1 theta_2 for each i = 1..o, so for any nu, nu' > 0: nu |B|_(o) + nu' |C|_(o) >= 2 o sqrt(nu nu' theta_1 theta_2). (c) At B = 0 this gives rank A + rank D <= k, and this exact form is rank B >= rank A + rank D - k.
statements.proof: (a) Lh = Diag + Off, with Diag the direct sum of the Ah_b, so Diag has at least k + o singular values above theta. Weyl: sigma_(k+j)(Diag) <= sigma_(k+1)(Lh) + sigma_j(Off) = sigma_j(Off). (b) Let U_A, W_A hold the singular vectors of A above theta_1, and U_D, W_D those of D above theta_2. Compress: M = [S_A Bt; Ct S_D], with S_A, S_D diagonal with entries above theta_1, theta_2, and Bt = U_A^T B W_D, Ct = U_D^T C W_A. rank M <= k. By the Schur complement, rank M = r_1 + rank(S_D - Z), Z = Ct S_A^-1 Bt. So rank(S_D - Z) <= r_2 - o. Weyl gives sigma_(r_2 - o + j)(S_D) <= sigma_j(Z), so sigma_o(Z) >= sigma_(r_2)(S_D) > theta_2. Horn's product inequality: sigma_o(Z) <= sigma_i(Ct) |S_A^-1|_op sigma_(o+1-i)(Bt) < sigma_i(Ct) sigma_(o+1-i)(Bt) / theta_1. Compression does not raise singular values. For the sum: nu sigma_(o+1-i)(B) + nu' sigma_i(C) >= 2 sqrt(nu nu' theta_1 theta_2) by AM-GM; add over i. (c) L = X Y^T: rank(X_1 Y_2^T) >= rank X_1 + rank Y_2 - k (Sylvester). QED. Gauge note: B -> eB, C -> C/e keeps D = C A^+ B, so no bound holds on B alone. The product is the right object. It is first-order sharp: for k = 1 and a 2 x 2 matrix, |b c| = |a d|.

statements.statement: Theorem G4 (kept families, shared budget: exact least at a loss above 0). Classes split into families H_1..H_J with |H_b| = K_b = 2 r_b >= 4, with a fixed-point-free pairing c <-> c' inside each. C = sum K_b, w = C/2 = sum r_b. Rows: regions A_c of P, one per class, with masses pi_c, and s_x = s_c on A_c. R_b = the union of A_c over c in H_b. Y = the span of the indicators of the R_b. L^Y(k) = inf over A' (C x J), V' (C x k), free codes c of sum p_x KL(s_x || softmax(A'[b(x)] + V' c_x)). Numbers: any offsets A_b in R^C, one per family; tau_b > 0, mu_b > 0 with mu_b tau_b = Y0 the same for all b. Write mu_c = mu_b / pi_c for c in H_b, q_c = softmax(A_b + tau_b (e_c - e_c')), q'_c = q_c[c'], m_c = the least of q_c[i] over all i != c' (strangers included), beta_b = 1/2 - 1/K_b, Pi*_b = (1/2)(I + swap) - 1_b 1_b^T / K_b on H_b, Pi* = their direct sum, s_c = q_c + mu_c Pi* e_c, phi(y) = (1+y) log(1+y) - y, gamma_c = 4 m_c phi(-mu_c/(2 m_c)), g_c(T) = (mu_c tau_b - gamma_c) T + gamma_c T^2 - q'_c phi(mu_c T / q'_c). Premises: (1) m_c >= mu_c / 2; (2) g_c >= 0 on [0, 1 - 1/K_b]. Let X = sum pi_c (H(q_c) - H(s_c)). Then: 1. L^Y(w) = X > 0, attained by units e_c - e_c' per pair, codes +-tau_b, offsets A_b. 2. For k <= w: L^Y(k) >= X + Y0 (w - k). 3. L_free(w) >= X >= L_free(w + J - 1), and X <= SHARE(w) with equality when the conditional of A_b on each H_b' does not depend on b. 4. If g_c > 0 on (0, 1 - 1/K_b], then every minimiser at k = w has J_F span(V') equal to the sum of the pole spaces, so family b receives exactly r_b units (J_F = the direct sum of the centrings on H_b). 5. mu_c <= 2 m_c and mu_c / m_c + log(1 + mu_c / q'_c) < tau_b are enough for g_c > 0, so any A_b and tau_b give members at small mu. 6. For J >= 2 the sum of TQ22 minors at k = w is 0, since w >= K_b - 1. 7. If kept units T have span(1, h_T) = Y on P, and each pair function (+1, -1 on the pair's regions, 0 elsewhere) is affine in z_S on P, then V_b(w) with T kept equals X.
statements.proof:
Upper side. KL(s_c || q_c) = H(q_c) - H(s_c) + <q_c - s_c, log q_c>, and <q_c - s_c, log q_c> = -mu_c e_c^T Pi* A_b, since Pi* kills 1 and e_c - e_c'. Multiply by pi_c and add over c in H_b: -mu_b 1_b^T Pi* A_b = 0. So the build's loss is X. X > 0 since s_c != q_c for K_b >= 4.
Lower side. Fix a competitor of rank k <= w. Let S0 = J_F col(V'), of dimension at most k. Let Pi be the orthogonal projector onto a subspace of dimension C - J - k of range(J_F) orthogonal to S0. Then Pi 1_b = 0 for each b, and Pi V' = 0, because V' differs from J_F V' by family-constant columns. Put q°_x = s_x - mu_c Pi e_c on A_c. Rows sum to 1. Feasibility: on R_b the sum of p_x mu_c <Pi e_c, A'_b> is mu_b <Pi 1_b, A'_b> = 0, and <Pi e_c, V' c_x> = 0. Weak duality (TQ13 part 1) gives D >= sum pi_c (H(q°_c) - H(s_c)). Write q°_c = q_c - mu_c f_c, f_c = (Pi - Pi*) e_c. By (E) of TQ17, H(q°_c) - H(q_c) = mu_c <log q_c, f_c> - sum over i of q_c[i] phi(-mu_c f_c[i] / q_c[i]).
Linear term. log q_c = A_b + tau_b (e_c - e_c') + const. The sum of f_c over c in H_b is (Pi - Pi*) 1_b = 0, so the A_b part vanishes, family by family. What is left is Y0 times the sum of (D_c + T_c), with D_c = Pi_cc - beta_b, T_c = beta_b - Pi_cc'. And sum D_c = tr Pi - sum K_b beta_b = (C - J - k) - (w - J) = w - k.
Entries. Pi <= J_F, so Pi_ci <= (1/4) |J_F (e_c + e_i)|^2. In one family this is beta_b; across families it is 1/2 - (1/K_b + 1/K_b')/4. So T_c >= 0. Also f_c[c] <= 1/2, in-family tail f = Pi_ci + 1/K_b <= 1/2, stranger f = Pi_ci <= 1/2, f_c[c'] = -T_c. T_c <= 1 - 1/K_b, since Pi_cc' >= -1/2.
Row identity. The sum of f_c[i]^2 is Pi_cc - 2 e_c^T Pi Pi* e_c + beta_b. Pi* e_c = (e_c + e_c')/2 - 1_b / K_b and Pi 1_b = 0, so it equals beta_b - Pi_cc' = T_c. So the sum over i != c' of f^2 is T_c - T_c^2.
Domain and cost. For i != c', mu_c f <= mu_c / 2 <= m_c <= q. The partner is only lifted, so a tiny q'_c is allowed. As in TQ17, phi(y)/y^2 decreases and q phi(-w/q) decreases in q, so q phi(-mu_c f / q) <= gamma_c f^2. So D >= X + Y0 (w - k) + sum pi_c g_c(T_c) >= X + Y0 (w - k). This is 1 and 2.
3. Offsets count as a kept part, so L_free(w) >= L^Y(w). For the other side, write A_b = A_1 + (A_b - A_1): J - 1 free columns with family-indicator codes hold all the offsets. SHARE(w) >= X: the same dual has zero sum on each family, so masses are kept and the chain rule gives the SHARE objective; offsets common across rows are a subset. Equality is the build.
4. Equality forces T_c = 0, so f_c = 0 by the row identity, so Pi = Pi*. If dim S0 < w, the complement holds more than one rank-(w - J) projector, and all would have to equal Pi*, which is impossible. So S0 is the sum of the pole spaces.
5. As TQ17 part 3. gamma_c <= mu_c^2 / m_c, q' phi(mu T / q') <= mu T log(1 + mu / q') for T <= 1, drop gamma T^2.
6. Each minor has K_b - 1 <= w, so it fits exactly.
7. Upper: always-on read units relu(m . z + beta) equal the pair function plus a constant on P; the constant goes into kept offsets. Lower: a network of this class has logits A' h_T + V' (unit values), a member of the class of L^Y(w). QED.
Comment. D2 reaches this same X with k units per family, because its strangers are copied from a shared build. Here strangers are set by offsets, and at k = w the units are not shared. The budget is one projector across all families: tr Pi = sum (r_b - 1).

statements.statement: Proposition G6 (no fixed vector closes the J - 1 gap on tiny partners). Setting of G4 at free codes, rank k = w + J - 1, with log q_c = t + M 1_b + tau (e_c - e_c') and common mu_c pi_c = mu, tau, M > 0. Consider a dual point q°_c = s_c - mu_c Pi g_c, with g_c fixed in advance (not depending on the competitor) and Pi* g_c = Pi* e_c, required to be a distribution for every projector Pi of rank C - 1 - k with Pi <= J. Then: 1. If this must hold as q'_c -> 0 at fixed mu_c, then J g_c = (2 Pi0 - J) e_c', the reflection of D4, that is Pi g_c = Pi (e_c - 2 * 1_b / K_b), where Pi0 = Pi*. 2. For this g_c, whenever Pi (e_c - e_c') = 0 for all c, the dual value is at most X - mu M sum_b 1_b^T Pi 1_b, so it is below X once Pi moves off the family indicators. 3. The other natural form, g_c = e_c, leaves the simplex at Pi = Pi* + P_F, where P_F is the projector on the family contrasts: the partner entry is q'_c - mu_c (1/K_b - 1/C), negative when mu_c / q'_c > 1 / (1/K_b - 1/C). So a certificate of L_free(w + J - 1) = X on these tables must have a dual that is not of this form. This is a limit on proofs, not on the value: fits say the value is X for large M.
statements.proof: 1. e_c'^T Pi g_c <= beta + q'/mu_c for all Pi, with equality at Pi* up to q'/mu_c, so as q' -> 0, Pi* is a maximum and is stationary. Rotate a unit xi in range(Pi*) towards a unit zeta in the complement inside 1^perp: the derivative of e_c'^T Pi g_c is (e_c' . xi)(zeta . g_c) + (e_c' . zeta)(xi . g_c) = 0 for all xi, zeta. With a = Pi* e_c', a' = (J - Pi*) e_c', h = Pi* g_c, h' = (J - Pi*) g_c, this says a tensor h' + h tensor a' = 0. a != 0 at K_b >= 4 and a' != 0. So h = lambda a and h' = -lambda a'. h = Pi* e_c = a gives lambda = 1. So J g_c = a - a' = (2 Pi* - J) e_c'. With y = (e_c - e_c')/2, z = Pi* e_c, a' = -y + 1_b/K_b - 1/C, so J g_c = z + y - 1_b/K_b + 1/C, and Pi g_c = Pi (e_c - 2 * 1_b / K_b), since e_c = z + y + 1_b/K_b. 2. The sum of g_c over c in H_b gives -Pi 1_b modulo the kernel. In the linear term: the t part is mu <-Pi 1, t> = 0; the M part is -mu M sum_b 1_b^T Pi 1_b; the tau part is mu tau sum 2 y^T Pi g_c = 0 when Pi y = 0, and the rotation of a family direction into range(Pi*) keeps Pi y = 0. The cost is >= 0. 3. At Pi* + P_F, e_c'^T Pi e_c = beta_b + 1/K_b - 1/C. QED.

statements.statement: Conjecture G7 (free codes, no kept units, flat M). In G4 with log q_c = t + M 1_b + tau (e_c - e_c'): (a) L_free(w + J - 1) = X whenever M is above a threshold of about log tau plus a constant. (b) At k = w: L_free(w) >= X + mu tau (J - 1) + mu M sum_b (K_b - K_b^2 / C). Route for (a): a dual that depends on the competitor, with rows v_c in range(Pi), v_c[c'] <= beta_b + q'_c / mu_c, and family sums Pi 1_b with weights that depend on the row. Rows whose partner has Pi 1_b entry <= 0 can carry the family move, as sketched in the note on row weights delta_c. Non-local competitors at rotation W about .1 to .25 must also be paid by the tail term q'' M^2 theta^2. Route for (b): the same, since the linear form is invalid by G6 part 3.

statements.statement: Theorem G2 (priced bound: rank shares plus a price for overflow). No kept units. Blocks S_1..S_J: each lists n_b rows and n_b classes as pairs (x_j, i_j), rows distinct, classes distinct; row sets of different blocks disjoint, class sets of different blocks disjoint. For a competitor L = 1 t^T + c V^T restricted to these rows and classes, let Lh = (direct sum of J_b) L (direct sum of J_b), unweighted centring per block, so rank Lh <= k. Let Ah_b be its diagonal blocks, Off the rest, and Toff the same part of the centred log table. nu = the least of p_x s_x[i] over off-block pairs. Parameters: theta > 0, beta, b in (0,1], x0 > 0, kappa_t = phi(-t)/t^2. Own numbers as in C10: Ybar_b = Y_b - a 1^T - 1 g^T, m_b = the least diagonal of Ybar_b, A_b = the symmetric off-diagonal part, k'' = r + 1 + n_b x0, and G_b(r) = (m_b - 1 - kappa_b b - theta)(n_b^2 / k'' - n_b) - (n_b / sqrt k'') |A_b|_(r+1), with G_b(r) = 0 if n_b <= k''. Let xi_b >= 0 satisfy xi_b <= b p s on off-diagonal pairs of block b and xi_b <= x0 p s on its diagonal pairs. Then L_free(k) >= the least over r in {0..k}^J of [ sum_b xi_b G_b(r_b)_+ + beta nu ( o (theta - kappa_beta beta) - |Toff|_(o) )_+ ], with o = (sum r_b - k)_+, and the second term 0 at o = 0.
statements.proof: Fix a competitor. Let r_b = the number of singular values of Ah_b above theta. Own part: A_h = the top r_b singular part of Ah_b; U = span(1, its left singular vectors), rank <= r_b + 1. C8 gives x, T, R^b = xi_b (D_x^-1 - T), symmetric, positive semidefinite (D_x^(1/2) R D_x^(1/2) = xi (I - projector)), with R^b U = 0, zero row and column sums. So <R^b, L_b> = <R^b, Ah_b - A_h> <= theta tr R^b, because |Ah_b - A_h|_op <= theta. The gain and cost steps are those of C10: <log s, R^b> >= m_b tr R^b - xi <A_b, T>, cost <= (1 + kappa_b b) tr R^b, <A_b, T> <= |A_b|_(r_b+1) sqrt(Sigma), Sigma = sum 1/x_l >= n_b^2 / k''. Net >= xi_b G_b(r_b); take xi_b = 0 at this competitor if that is negative. Price part: if o >= 1, let E = Off - Toff and Uh = the sum over j <= o of u_j v_j^T for E's top singular pairs; these vectors have zero sum on each block. Let Uoff be Uh with diagonal blocks removed, and R^off = -beta nu Uoff. |Uh_xi| <= 1 gives |R^off| <= beta nu <= beta p s. Row sums and column sums on each block are 0, so <R^off, log s - L> = beta nu <Uoff, E> = beta nu |E|_(o) >= beta nu (|Off|_(o) - |Toff|_(o)) >= beta nu (o theta - |Toff|_(o)) by Lemma G1 (a). Cost: p s phi(-R / (p s)) <= kappa_beta R^2 / (p s) <= kappa_beta beta^2 nu Uoff^2, in total at most kappa_beta beta^2 nu o, since |Uoff|_F^2 <= o. Dual point: R = sum R^b + R^off, on disjoint entries, so s - R/p is a distribution. Weak duality in the form D >= <log s - L, R> - sum p s phi(-R/(p s)) gives the sum. Minimise over the shares r. QED.

statements.statement: Corollary G2.1 (when G2 is a true knapsack, and how this differs from TQ2.3). Under G2 with |Toff|_(o) <= o tau for all o, let P = beta nu (theta - kappa_beta beta - tau) and Delta = the largest over b and r >= floor(k/J) of xi_b (G_b(r)_+ - G_b(r+1)_+). If P >= Delta, then L_free(k) >= the least over sum r_b <= k of sum_b xi_b G_b(r_b)_+. Difference from TQ2.3: there the between-node entries are e^(-m), so nu -> 0, P -> 0, and the premise fails: one unit serves two nodes at a cost on the scale of the strangers' mass. The knapsack is not false in general; it needs strangers at least as heavy, per entry, as the residual price of one unit. With the peak own term of C10 the premise needs nu (theta - 1) >= xi (m' - theta) (K/k)^2, and with nu <= xi this holds only at theta near m', where the own term is near 0.
statements.proof: Take any r with o >= 1. Some r_b > k/J. Lowering it by 1 raises the own term by at most Delta and lowers the price by exactly P (the price is linear in o at this bound). Repeat until o = 0. For TQ2.3: a block of size 2 has own rank 1 and strangers of order e^(-m), so G2's price is of order e^(-m) m. The last sentence: Delta is about xi (m' - theta)(n J / k)^2 at r = k/J. QED.

statements.statement: Theorem G3 (partition block: a knapsack in rank shares at the scale of the block's smallest entry). In Theorem C10 let a block S carry a partition P_1..P_y of its positions, and take r = y + k with no other kept part. Replace Ybar by Y - sum_b 1_(P_b) u_b^T - sum_b v_b 1_(P_b)^T, for any vectors u_b, v_b, and let A^P, m_S be read from it. Then L_free(k) >= the sum over S of xi_S G^P_S(k), with G^P_S = m' (n^2 / k'' - n) - (n / sqrt k'') |A^P_S|_(r), k'' = r + n x0. And n^2 / k'' is the least over shares rho_b >= 0 with sum rho_b <= k'' of the sum over b of |P_b|^2 / rho_b, so the first term is a knapsack in shares of one Lewis position, r in total. On the two-level table (top a, relatives b1, strangers b2, J families of f, K = J f) A^P = 0 and L_free(k) >= p b2 (log(a/b1) - 2)(K^2 / (k + J + K b2/a) - K).
statements.proof: C10's proof with U_S = the span of the indicators of the P_b and the codes on S, rank <= y + k, and 1 in its range. R^S is symmetric and R^S U = 0, so it kills 1_(P_b) on both sides, and <log s, R^S> = <Ybar, R^S> for the new Ybar. Nothing else changes. Lewis shares: rho_b = the sum of x_j over j in P_b, sum rho_b = sum x_j <= k''; Cauchy on each part gives the sum of 1/x_j >= sum_b |P_b|^2 / rho_b. QED. How it differs from C10's blocks: the rank is one budget across all parts, and relatives no longer enter a penalty. The cost is r = y + k and m_S falling from log(a/b2) to log(a/b1). The scale is the block's smallest entry: every off-diagonal entry is capped by xi. So at tiny strangers the bound goes to 0, in agreement with B6 and TQ2.3.

statements.statement: Proposition G5 (upper side of the price). Let rows split as R_b and classes as H_b. Let (t_b, V_b, c_b) be minimisers of the minors of TQ22 at k units, stacked into t, V, c. Then L_free(k + J - 1) <= SHARE(k) <= sum_b L^(b)(k) + sum over b != b', x in R_b of p_x s_x(H_b') KL(s_x | H_b' || softmax(t_b' + V_b' c_x)). For strangers uniform on H_b', that KL is at most the largest minus the mean of V_b' c_x over classes, so it is at most |c_x|_2 times 2 max_i |V_b'[i]|_2, and the gauge c_b -> c_b / l_b, V_b -> l_b V_b may be chosen. So the price of sharing is at most (stranger mass) times (the write size between blocks), to compare with the floor nu o (theta - 1) of G2.

statements.proof: Why it failed. Any dual whose R12 block is nonzero has R12 <= p s on stranger entries at positive R, because a competitor can lower a stranger's logit at slope p s only. Columns of R on H_1 satisfy: the moment on R_1 equals minus the moment on R_2. If R_2's entries are lifts only, the moment on R_1 must lie in the cone over R_2's codes. A competitor that places each family's codes in a tight far cluster (D2's A mu_j) narrows that cone to about one ray, so the block dual sees about r - 1 units, not r / J. That competitor pays only on strangers: stranger mass times the write size, by G1 and G5. Peak-level arithmetic: with xi at the relatives' scale and nu per stranger entry, the L1 price of full overlap is about 2 nu m n^2 / r, the same as C10's sum of family blocks plus one union block. So on peak tables the coupled form adds no power over C10's LP unless the union block's penalty kills it, which is where G3 helps. Second cause in G2: the price uses |E|_1 >= |E|_*. For spread singular vectors this loses a factor of about n / r. The factor is real only for incoherent competitors: a coherent competitor makes the two norms equal. A Lewis-weighted test matrix or the gamma_2 dual form min |D_a^-1 B D_b^-1|_op should recover it, but its coupling to own terms is not worked out.

result.blocked_by: A proof of Conjecture G7 (a) needs a dual point at free codes that stays a distribution with a partner tiny against mu_c, while Pi does not kill the family indicators. Proposition G6 shows that a fixed vector g_c in s_c - mu_c Pi g_c must be the reflection of D4, and that form has family term -mu M sum 1_b^T Pi 1_b, which goes below X at a rotation of a family direction into range(Pi*). So the step that stops me is writing rows v_c in range(Pi), depending on the competitor, with v_c[c'] <= beta_b, with family sums carrying +Pi 1_b, and with a row-wise cost that M pays. result.summary: The k new top units of a small network share one information budget: for any table with s_x >= e sbar, L_free(k) >= I(row; class) - k log(1/e), and the least equals I(s) minus the largest information a rank-k fit can keep, so this floor charges for sharing across all rows. On the level table with m classes the least is bracketed as I - k log(1/e') <= L_table(k) <= I - (k/2) log(1/(1 - theta^2)) + e'^(-k)/m, which proves F10(a) with slope exactly 1 - e, and fits match the upper end to 3 or 4 digits, so I state that end as a conjecture, not a theorem. Hardness stays open: the uniform chain at k = 1 is false, counting cannot give a no-go, and the reduction at k = 3 stops at one named rounding step, so this round fills no slot.

statements.statement: K1 (exact information dual; under: none). Rows x with weights p_x, positive table s, sbar = sum p_x s_x, I(s) = sum p_x KL(s_x || sbar). Fix V (C x k). A coupling for V is a list of rows pi_x on the simplex with (i) sum p_x pi_x = sbar and (ii) V^T pi_x = V^T s_x for every x. Then for every t, c, with l_x = t + V c_x, and every coupling pi: sum p_x KL(s_x || softmax(l_x)) >= sum p_x [H(pi_x) - H(s_x)] = I(s) - I(pi). Equality holds when pi_x = softmax(l_x), and at any stationary point in t and c the fit is itself a coupling. So L_free(k) = inf over V of [I(s) - min over couplings of I(pi)]. The same holds on region tables, so for L_table(k).
statements.proof: With A = log-sum-exp, KL(s||softmax(l)) = A(l) - <s,l> - H(s). Sum over x. By (i), sum p_x <s_x - pi_x, t> = 0. By (ii), sum p_x <s_x - pi_x, V c_x> = 0. So the loss equals sum p_x [A(l_x) - <pi_x, l_x> - H(s_x)]. Gibbs gives A(l) - <pi,l> >= H(pi), with equality at pi = softmax(l). The conditions (i), (ii) are the stationarity conditions in t and c for q = softmax(l), so a stationary q is a coupling and equality holds. Marginal sbar is common, so H(pi|X) - H(s|X) = I(s) - I(pi). Equality of the inf and the max at fixed V: the coupling problem is a concave maximum under linear constraints, and s is an interior feasible point, so Fenchel duality has no gap. Read as a network: for a chosen head V, the dual point is a distribution on classes that depends on V, it handles tiny classes through entropy, and the marginal constraint (i) couples rows of all blocks. These are the three properties the common block asked for. The min over V is not convex, so a lower bound at k must give a coupling for every V. That is what K2 does.

statements.statement: K2 (information floor; sharper F4; under: none). Let s be a positive table on any finite rows, sbar = sum p_x s_x, and 0 < e <= min over x, i of s_x[i] / sbar[i]. If e = 1 the table is constant and the claim is trivial. Otherwise, for every k >= 0: L_free(k) >= I(s) - k log(1/e). Since every code class and the unit form lie inside free codes, L_table (at T empty), L_on and V_b(k) with T empty obey the same floor. With kept units of rank y, replace k by k + y.
statements.proof: Let theta = 1 - e, beta = e/theta, so 1 + beta = 1/theta. Write nu = sbar and s_x = e nu + theta r_x, with r_x a distribution and sum p_x r_x = nu. Fix t, V. Write f_c(i) = t'_i + b_i . c, with t' = t - log nu, b_i the row i of V. Shift by row constants so that <nu, t'> = 0 and <nu, b> = 0. Let psi(c) = log <nu, exp f_c>. Restrict to the span of the b_i, of dimension k' <= k. Since all nu_i > 0 and 0 is in the relative interior of conv(b), psi is coercive and strictly convex. Step 1: KL(s_x || softmax(log nu + f_c)) = KL(s_x||nu) - <s_x, f_c> + psi(c) = KL(s_x||nu) - theta <r_x, f_c> + psi(c). So loss >= I(s) - Phi, with Phi = sum p_x sup_c [theta <r_x, f_c> - psi(c)] = sum p_x psi*(eta_x), eta_x = theta <r_x, b>, because sum p_x <r_x, t'> = <nu, t'> = 0. Each eta_x lies in the relative interior of conv(b), so a maximiser c_x exists with grad psi(c_x) = eta_x. Step 2: let G_x(c) = <r_x, f_c> - (1+beta) psi(c). Then sup G_x = Gamma_x = <r_x,t'> + psi*(eta_x)/theta and G_x(c) = Gamma_x - (1/theta) D(c, c_x), with D the Bregman distance D(c, c_x) = psi(c) - psi(c_x) - eta_x . (c - c_x). Jensen gives exp <r_x, f> <= <r_x, exp f>, so sum p_x exp G_x(c) <= <nu, exp f_c> exp(-(1+beta) psi(c)) = exp(-beta psi(c)). Step 3: integrate over c. With Z = integral of exp(-beta psi) and I_x = integral of exp(-(1/theta) D(c, c_x)): sum p_x exp(Gamma_x) I_x <= Z. Jensen gives sum p_x Gamma_x + sum p_x log I_x <= log Z. And sum p_x Gamma_x = Phi / theta. Step 4 (contraction): put c = c_x + e (w - c_x). D is convex in its first slot and 0 at c_x, so D(c, c_x) <= e D(w, c_x), and (1/theta) e = beta. So I_x >= e^(k') V_x, with V_x = integral of exp(-beta D(w, c_x)) dw. Step 5: V_x = Z E_P exp(beta [psi(c_x) + eta_x . (w - c_x)]), with P proportional to exp(-beta psi). Jensen gives log(V_x / Z) >= beta [eta_x . wbar - psi*(eta_x)], wbar the mean of P. Since sum p_x eta_x = theta <nu, b> = 0: -sum p_x log V_x <= -log Z + beta Phi. Step 6: Phi/theta <= k' log(1/e) + beta Phi, and 1/theta - beta = 1. So Phi <= k' log(1/e) <= k log(1/e). QED. Kept units: A h_T + V c has rank at most y + k, so it is a free-code logit of that rank. Read as a network: a tail the row must keep is a penalty on sharp codes, and it limits how many classes k units can tell apart, across all rows at once. The floor is 0 unless k < about I / log(1/e). Mostly I <= log K, so it covers coarse zooms (small k), not k = 14 at K = 1000.

statements.statement: K2b (corollaries of K2). (a) Alpha form: with r_x as in K2, for every alpha in [e, 1]: L_free(k) >= I(s) - (1 - alpha) I(r) - alpha k log(alpha/e). The best alpha is e exp(I(r)/k - 1) when that lies in [e, 1], and then L_free(k) >= I(s) - I(r) + k alpha. (b) F4's table, no size premise: with s_j[j] = 1 - e, s_j[i] = e u_ji, u_ji in [e^(-b), e^b]/(m-1), and w = 1 + e(e^b - 1): L_free(k) >= (1 - e) log m - h(e) - log w - k (log(1/e) + b + log w). (c) F5 sharper: the gap in its pair of tables grows like (1 - e) log m, not bounded by (1 - 4e)/16, and starts at m about exp(k (log(1/e) + b) / (1 - e)), far below F4's exp(c (k+2)^(3/2) / e). (d) Minors: with TQ22, L_free(k) >= sum over b of w_b [I_b - k log(1/e_b)]_+. Each block still gets all k there. Only a single block charges for sharing inside it.
statements.proof: (a) psi* is convex and theta <r_x,b> = (1 - alpha) <r_x,b> + alpha (1 - e/alpha) <r_x,b>. So Phi <= (1 - alpha) sum p_x psi*(<r_x,b>) + alpha sum p_x psi*((1 - e/alpha) <r_x,b>). The second sum is at most k log(alpha/e): it is K2's bound on Phi for the table (1 - e/alpha) r_x + (e/alpha) nu, which has floor e/alpha and the same marginal. The first: Gibbs gives psi(c) >= <r_x, f_c> - KL(r_x||nu), so <r_x, t'> + psi*(<r_x,b>) <= KL(r_x||nu), and sum p_x <r_x,t'> = 0. Differentiate in alpha for the optimum. (b) sbar[i] <= w/m, so H(sbar) >= log m - log w. H(s_j) <= h(e) + e log(m-1). So I >= (1 - e) log m - h(e) - log w. For the floor, s_j[i]/sbar[i] >= e e^(-b) m/((m-1) w) >= e e^(-b)/w off the diagonal, and the diagonal is larger for m >= 2. (c) Put (b) against F3's table s0, as in F5. (d) TQ22 plus K2 on each minor.

statements.statement: K3 (Gaussian build; F10(a) with c = 1 - e). Let m rows = m classes, weights 1/m, s_j = theta delta_j + e' u, u uniform, theta = 1 - e'. For every k >= 1: L_table(k) <= I - (k/2) log(1/(1 - theta^2)) + e'^(-k)/m, with I = KL(s_j||u) = log m - H(s_j). With K2: I - k log(1/e') <= L_table(k). So for fixed e', k, as m grows, L_table(k) / log m tends to 1 - e, e = e'(m-1)/m the tail mass, not to F4's order e M / k^(3/2). This proves F10(a).
statements.proof: Draw b_i in R^k iid N(0, I). Let Pi = 1/(1 - theta^2), r' = theta^2 Pi, rho = Pi theta. Let t_i = (k - |b_i|^2) r'/2, so E t = 0, and let c_j = rho b_j. Let psi(c) = log E exp(t + b . c) = k r'/2 - (k/2) log Pi + |c|^2/(2 Pi), and f_i(c) = t_i + b_i . c. Row loss: KL(s_j||softmax f) = I - <s_j, f(c_j)> + log((1/m) sum over i of exp f_i(c_j)). Given b_j, Jensen on the other points gives E log(...) <= psi(c_j) + log(1 + r_j/m), with r_j = exp(f_j(c_j) - psi(c_j)) = Pi^(k/2) exp(|b_j|^2 theta/(1+theta)). And E f_i(c_j) = 0 for i != j, so E <s_j, f(c_j)> = (theta + e'/m) E f_j(c_j) >= theta rho k. Sum: -theta rho k + k r'/2 + rho^2 k/(2 Pi) = 0, by r' = theta^2 Pi and rho = Pi theta, leaving -(k/2) log Pi. Last: E log(1 + r/m) <= E r / m, and E r = Pi^(k/2) ((1+theta)/(1-theta))^(k/2) = (1-theta)^(-k) = e'^(-k). Some draw is at or below the mean. QED. Read as a network: class weights in a head of k units form a Gaussian cloud, each class gets its own spot, a photo's code sits near its class, and k units tell apart about (1/(1-theta^2))^(k/2) groups of classes.

statements.statement: K4 (the Gaussian cap). For every table with floor e and theta = 1 - e, and every k: L_free(k) >= I(s) - (k/2) log(1/(1 - theta^2)). Equivalently, for affine functions h_x on R^k with weights p_x and mean zero, and psi = log sum p_y exp h_y: sum p_x sup_c [theta h_x(c) - psi(c)] <= (k/2) log(1/(1 - theta^2)). Equivalently: for points b in R^k with law nu, there is a coupling (X, Y), both with law nu, with E[b_Y | X] = theta b_X and I(X;Y) <= (k/2) log(1/(1 - theta^2)). With K3 this would give L_table(k) = I - (k/2) log(1/(1 - theta^2)) up to e'^(-k)/m on the level table, a closed form at every k from two numbers.
statements.proof: Not proved. Route and what is proved. (1) Reduction: any table reduces to the case of delta rows mixed with the marginal, with weights p_x, since K2 Step 2's Jensen gives psi >= log sum p_x exp <r_x, f>; so tail != weights adds nothing, and the equivalent form is what must be shown. The coupling form is K1 with the minimax over t. (2) The bound K2 has k log(1/e), and is off by a factor 2 at small e. The loss is in Step 4 (a contraction, tight only for a cone-shaped D) and in Step 5 (Jensen, loose for a quadratic D). (3) Gaussian nu attains the cap: K3. (4) Expected at small theta, formal expansion for k = 1, unit variance, not a proof: R = theta^2/2 - theta^3 kappa3^2/6 + theta^4 (1/4 - kappa4^2/24) for kappa3 = 0, so Gaussian is the local maximum among all nu. (5) Lemma proved for theta near 1, smooth nu, k = 1: with R(z) = integral from z of y rho(y) dy and Stein kernel tau = R/rho, Var f(X) <= E[tau f'(X)^2] (Cacoullos; Cauchy-Schwarz on the double integral of (f(x) - f(y))^2), so U = integral of db/sqrt(tau) has Var U <= 1, h(U) <= (1/2) log(2 pi e), and so h(nu) <= (1/2) log(2 pi e) + (1/2) E log tau. A diffusion heuristic shows this is what the cap asks as theta -> 1; that link is not proved. (6) Why simple transports fail: Gaussian coupling through a Brenier map or stochastic localisation has the right information but E[b_Y|X] is not linear in b_X. A birth-death chain with generator L b = -b exists on any k = 1 point set, with spectral gap exactly 1 (b is monotone, so it is the first eigenfunction), and is a valid coupling, but I have no upper bound on its information.

statements.statement: K5 (the chain at k = 1 is not uniform; bad-row price). Let k = 1, classes with distinct b_i, tail mass zeta in the row. (a) Let a row be uniform on a pair {u, v} up to the tail, and let i_1, ..., i_(d-1) be the classes between them in b order. Suppose each consecutive pair on the chain from u to v has a row that is good in F7's sense at margin M. Then KL(row) >= (1 - zeta)(M/8)(d - 1) - H(s). (b) Among chains meeting margin M in the consecutive rows, a uniform chain has long-row price at least about M d^2/8 - log 2, while a two-sided geometric chain with ratio rho >= 2 has price at most (M/2)(d - 1) rho/(rho - 1) + log(C/2). So the price is Theta(M d) and the uniform chain is off by a factor of order d. So F7's option 'the optimal chain is uniform under heavy rows' is false in the form tested: with heavy path rows and one light long row, at large M, the two-sided geometric chain beats the uniform one.
statements.proof: (a) KL = -H(s) + A(l) - <s,l>, and l_i <= A(l) on the tail, so KL >= -H(s) + (1 - zeta)[A(l) - (l_u + l_v)/2]. Let m be the b-midpoint of u, v. The polygon of l through consecutive classes is affine in c at m with the same slope as the chord, so A(l) - (l_u + l_v)/2 >= polygon(t)(m) - (t_u + t_v)/2 = Sag, with no c left. With gaps g_j, slopes sigma_j and drops Delta_j = sigma_(j-1) - sigma_j, F7's good conditions on rows j - 1 and j give Delta_j >= M/g_(j-1) - M/(2 g_j) and Delta_j >= M/g_j - M/(2 g_(j-1)); adding gives Delta_j >= (M/4)(1/g_(j-1) + 1/g_j) > 0. So t is concave there and Sag = sum Delta_j G(m, b_j), with G(m, y) = (1/2) min(y - b_u, b_v - y). Each interior j has distance at least the adjacent gap on its near side, so Delta_j G >= M/8. Sum over d - 1 interior points. Good rows have no class between their pair, so the chain is consecutive. (b) Uniform: Delta = M, sag M d^2/8. Geometric: gaps grow by rho to the centre and fall back, Delta_j = M/min(g_(j-1), g_j), each row keeps margin M since t is concave. Choose c with l_u = l_v. Then A - l_u <= max l - l_u + log C = Sag at the top + log C, and each interior term is at most (M/2) rho/(rho-1), since a geometric sum of gaps is at most rho/(rho-1) times its largest term. Heavy rows then cost at most log(1 + (C - 2) e^(-M)) in both. Read as a network: along a chain of relatives, the units crowd the classes at the ends and spread those in the middle, so one far relative costs a length and not a length squared.

statements.statement: K6 (the reduction at fixed k >= 3, and the exact step where it stops). Table: rows uniform on sets S_x, tail exactly 0 (closed simplex, F1). ZERO(k) is the question L_table(k) = 0. Proved: (a) if each S_x is exactly a face of the upper hull of points (b_i, t_i) in R^(k+1), ZERO(k) holds; (b) if ZERO(k) holds then for every r > 0 there are points with, for each row, a functional with S_x values within delta and all other classes at least M below, 2 delta/M <= r, and for any two rows S, S' and any point p in both hulls, at least one of the two convex forms of p has mass at most r off S and S''s common part (an r-quasi-embedding); (c) F3: ZERO(k) holds for all set systems with |S_x| <= (k+1)/2, so a hard instance must have |S_x| >= (k+3)/2; for k = 3 that means sets of at least 3. Expected, not proved: the exact-face problem at k = 3 is existential-reals hard, through Richter-Gebert's universality of 4-polytopes, with rows the facets but one. NOT proved: hardness of L_table(k).
statements.proof: (a) Scale logits by lambda -> infinity: every row's top set dominates and the loss tends to 0. (b) Loss near 0 and Pinsker give small delta and large M. Let p be in both hulls with forms alpha, alpha', heights h, h'. If h >= h': sum alpha_i l_y(i) = h + p . c_y >= h' + p . c_y >= level_y - delta, as in F6(a). But alpha's mass mu off S' sits at least M below the level and the rest is at most level + delta, so level + delta - mu M >= level - delta, and mu <= 2 delta/M. The case h <= h' is the same with x. (c) F3. Where it stops: (i) passing from all r > 0 to an exact realisation. The sets of r-quasi-embeddings are not compact, since scale and point collisions are free, and an exact incidence may fail while approximations survive. The missing statement is a rounding lemma: there is r0(K) > 0 such that an r0-quasi-embedding of a complex K gives an exact face realisation. (ii) Without (i), a no instance may still have L = 0. (iii) The same rounding is what would bridge to EMBED(2 to 3), which is NP-hard (de Mesmay, Rieck, Sedgwick, Tancer, recalled); that route also needs yes instances to be linear and regular after a subdivision computed without the solution. Explicit tails also need margin bits (F7b). At k = 1, a threshold test needs an exact function of arrangement and gaps. K5 shows the price is Theta(M d) with a free chain, so 2-SUM is not it, and a bandwidth gap has no sum form. What a proof must use: a table family where approximate faces force exact faces, or exact prices for bounded structures.

statements.statement: K7 (counting cannot give a no-go against polynomial claims). Let r = min(K, C) - 1. (a) At precision delta, the number of functions k -> L_table(k) on any tables with K rows and C classes is at most binom(N + r, r) with N = ceil(log C / delta), so about r log2(e (1 + N/r)) bits. (b) There is a family of near-uniform positive tables, with K = C, on which at least binom(N' + r - 1, r) of them are distinct at precision g eps^2/(4 K C), for any integer N' and grid g, as eps -> 0. So a claim complete for this family must hold about r log2(N'/r) bits, and that many are also enough to write the profile down. So: the count is Theta(r log(1/delta)), polynomial, and no bit count separates a polynomial claim from the profile. Any no-go must use checkability, not information.
statements.proof: (a) L_table is non-increasing in k, at most log C, and 0 for k >= r; count non-increasing grid sequences. (b) s = softmax(eps A), A with zero row and column means and squared singular values w_i in g {1..N'}, non-increasing, equal row weights. Upper: KL at uniform has Taylor form (1/(2C)) |P(x - y)|^2 + O(cube), and the truncated SVD is a rank-k logit, so L(k) <= (eps^2/(2 K C)) sum over i > k of w_i (1 + o(1)). Lower: a best competitor has loss O(eps^2), Pinsker gives q_x within O(eps) in L1 of s_x, so q is near uniform with centred logits O(eps), and the Taylor form holds uniformly; offset plus code has affine rank k, and Eckart-Young on column-centred A gives the same value. The grid is finite, so eps can be chosen uniformly. Distinct sequences differ at some tail sum by at least g, so at precision g eps^2/(4 K C) their profiles differ. Read as a network: a nearly undecided network's small head is its top singular directions, so each size is a separate fact about N, but only one number each.

statements.statement: K8 (slot 1 and slot 3 at every k: the conditional form of a no-go). Let F be a class of tables on which deciding L_table(k) <= theta is NP-hard. Suppose a claim type has polynomial-time error, each table of F has a polynomial-size claim of the type with error 0, and from such a claim a closed form computes L_table(k) in polynomial time for every k. Then P = NP. If the closed form may cost more, but a polynomial witness of the value is checkable, then NP = coNP. Without either form of checkable value, F9 stands: no contradiction arises, since the trunk allows a one-time computation of any cost. The premise is NOT proved for any class: see K6. So this is a conditional, and no no-go on a clean instance is proved. Also: K2's floor claim shows a size-free claim can bound every k, and K4 would give a two-number claim that determines the least at every k with e'^(-k) far below m, on the level table.
statements.proof: A claim is found outside the trunk, so it is a witness: guess it, check error 0 in polynomial time, and compute the value. This puts the decision problem and its complement in NP, or in P when the claim can be computed too. Precisely: with a polynomial closed form and a claim that is guessed, both L <= theta and L > theta are in NP, so hardness gives NP = coNP; P = NP needs in addition that the claim is computed from the table. Correction to the statement above: from guessing alone one obtains NP = coNP, and P = NP only if the claim can be found in polynomial time. How M is found is outside the trunk, so the correct conclusion is NP = coNP.

result.track: J: the read is the real object (L_on and V_b)
result.summary: For the always-on read, I replaced E6's 2 g^2 / eta by the true ratio, gave a graded form in defects, and proved an exact read cost at a binding rank: on a pole table whose rows have within-class variation, L_on(k) has a closed form and at confidence L_on / L_free tends to 1 + K (1/y_min - 1). For the gated box, I proved that the read is usually not V_b: at k >= 2, L_on = V_b needs V^T r = 0 on every hull vertex row, and on the same pole table a gate removes all of the read cost, so V_b(k) = L_free(k) < L_on(k), with a jump as y_min -> 0. New exact statements reach V_b through an indicator claim, and one k = 1 family has V_b = L_on > L_free, but all exact tables here are toy-world or perturbative, so no slot is filled, and no lower bound on V_b above L_free exists yet for dense within-class variation.

statements.statement: J1 (sharp moment certificate). Setting of E6: rows p_x > 0, s_x > 0; zeta_x in R^D p-orthonormal, first y coordinates span Y, 1 in Y; competitors l'_x = B' zeta_x, B' = [A' | V' M'], rank V' <= k. Triple B_0 = [A_0 | V M_0], V^T V = I, V^T 1 = 0, M_0 of rank k, least singular value sigma, C >= k + 2, q = softmax(B_0 zeta). Gamma_0 = sum p (s - q) zeta^T = [0 | Gamma], V^T Gamma = 0, Gamma M_0^T = 0. D_0 = D(triple). Psi(B) = sum p Cov(q_x) B zeta_x zeta_x^T on {1^T B = 0}, eta its least eigenvalue. <<X>> = <[0|X], Psi^-1 [0|X]>. For a rank m = C-1-k projector Pi with Pi 1 = 0, V'^T Pi = 0: Pi_0 = J - V V^T, E = Pi - Pi_0, S = V^T Pi V, X = tr S. For any (D-y) x k matrix W, which may depend on Pi: R_W = Gamma + V W^T, Omega = W^T M_0^T. Then: (1) If q° are row distributions with sum p (q° - q) zeta^T = [0 | -E R_W], then D(l') >= D_0 + tr(S Omega) - sum p KL(q° || q). (2) Fisher point: F = Psi^-1 [0 | -E R_W], f_x = F zeta_x, g_x = f_x - <q_x, f_x>, q° = q(1 + g). If g_x >= -a with a in (0,1] on all rows, the cost is at most c(a) <<E R_W>>, with c(a) = phi(-a)/a^2 = integral over t in [0,1] of (1-t)/(1-t a), c(0+) = 1/2, c(1) = 1. (3) So if for every Pi: g >= -a and c(a) <<E R_W>> <= tr(S Omega), then L_Z(k) = D_0. Without the second condition: D_0 - L_Z(k) <= sup over Pi of (c(a) <<E R_W>> - tr(S Omega))_+. (4) With W = w Btil, Btil = M_0^T (M_0 M_0^T)^-1: Omega = w I. The true ratio is tau(w) = sup over Pi of <<E R_w>> / X, and the test is c(a) tau(w) <= w. Pi by Pi, with A_1 = <<E Gamma>>, A_2 = <<E V Btil^T>>, A_12 their Psi^-1 inner product, a w >= 0 exists exactly when X - 2 c A_12 >= 2 c sqrt(A_1 A_2). (5) Chain: tau(w) <= 2 lambda_max(A_w) <= 2 max(g^2, w^2/sigma^2) / eta, where A_w is the form E -> <<E R_w>> on symmetric E with E 1 = 0, tr E = 0. At w = g sigma, c = 1 this is E6's first condition. E6's second condition implies a <= 1. Also a can be taken as sqrt(2 k*) times the largest over x, i of the Frobenius norm of the symmetric matrix that represents the linear map E -> g_x[i].
statements.proof: Fenchel: A(l') >= <q°, l'> + H(q°) for a distribution q°, with A the log-sum-exp. So D(l') >= sum p (H(q°) - H(s)) + sum p <q° - s, l'>. Moment of q° - s: [0 | -E R - Gamma] = [0 | -Pi R], since Pi_0 R = Gamma (V^T Gamma = 0, 1^T Gamma = 0, Pi_0 V = 0). Against B' = [A' | V' M'] this is -tr(R^T Pi V' M') = 0. So D(l') >= sum p (H(q°) - H(s)). H(q°) - H(q) = -<log q, q° - q> - KL(q°||q). log q_x = B_0 zeta_x - (log Z_x) 1, and q° - q is orthogonal to 1. So the linear sum is <V M_0, E R> = tr(M_0^T V^T E Gamma) + tr(M_0^T V^T E V W^T) = tr(V^T E Gamma M_0^T) + tr(S W^T M_0^T) = tr(S Omega), using Gamma M_0^T = 0 and V^T Pi_0 = 0. D_0 = sum p (H(q) - H(s)) - <Gamma_0, B_0> and <Gamma_0, B_0> = 0. This gives (1). (2): Cov(q_x) f_x = q_x g_x entrywise, so the moment is Psi(F) = [0 | -E R]. KL(q°||q) = E_q phi(g). phi(y) = y^2 times the integral of (1-t)/(1+t y), which decreases in y, so phi(y) <= c(a) y^2 for y >= -a. E_q g^2 = Var_q(f), and sum p Var_q(f_x) = <F, Psi F> = <<E R>>. (3), (4): direct. Minimising c(A_1 + 2 w A_12 + w^2 A_2) - w X over w gives w* = (X - 2 c A_12)/(2 c A_2), and the value is <= 0 exactly when the stated inequality holds, given w* >= 0. (5): |E|_F^2 = 2 X, so <<E R>> <= lambda_max |E|_F^2. Also <<Y>> <= |Y|_F^2 / eta and |E R|_F <= |E|_F |R|_op, with |R_w|_op = max(g, w/sigma) by the orthogonality on both sides. g_x[i] is linear in E, so its size is at most |E|_F times that Frobenius norm, and X <= k*.

statements.statement: J1-local (the exact row-whitened number). With (K, N, A), K of C x k with K^T V = 0 and K^T 1 = 0, let dB = [A | K M_0 + V N] and rho_H = sup of 2 <Gamma, K N> / <dB, Psi dB>. This is a generalized eigenvalue problem, polynomial in size. (1) Along (V + eps K)(M_0 + eps N), A_0 + eps A: D - D_0 = eps^2 [ (1/2) <dB, Psi dB> - <Gamma, K N> ] + o(eps^2). So rho_H > 1 means the triple is not a local least of L_Z(k), and rho_H < 1 means it is a strict local least. (2) If the test of J1 holds at all spans near V, with a fixed W, then rho_H <= 1. So the test is a strengthening of the true necessary condition, and c -> 1/2 is the correct constant. (3) Whitened form. C_bar = sum p Cov(q_x), Psi_0 = C_bar tensor I, ell the largest number with Psi >= ell Psi_0. Gamma_t = C_bar^(+1/2) Gamma, Kept_t = C_bar^(1/2) V M_0 = V_t M_t, g_t = |Gamma_t|_op, sigma_t = the least singular value of M_t, varsigma = g_t / sigma_t. Then V_t^T Gamma_t = 0 and Gamma_t M_t^T = 0, so the two parts are an SVD split of a Newton target. If the whitened dual point stays >= -a: D(l') >= D_0 + X_t g_t (sigma_t - 2 c(a) g_t / ell), so varsigma <= ell / (2 c(a)) with positivity gives L_Z(k) = D_0. (4) If Psi = Psi_0, then rho_H = varsigma and ell = 1. Then the test reaches varsigma <= 1 as a -> 0, the Eckart-Young threshold. (5) In general varsigma > 1 is NOT proved to break the triple. So the numbers 197, 18, 3.8, 1.1 of LADDER 47 give no failure by themselves, if they equal varsigma. I did not recompute them.
statements.proof: (1) TQ20: D(l') - D(l) = sum p KL(q||q') - sum p <s - q, l' - l>. KL is (1/2) <dB, Psi dB> at second order. By stationarity only the eps^2 K N term of the moment survives. <dB, Psi dB> = 0 forces A = 0 and K M_0 + V N = 0, so K = 0 (K^T V = 0 and M_0 has full row rank) and N = 0. (2) At small eps, E = -eps (K V^T + V K^T) + O(eps^2), S = eps^2 K^T K + O(eps^4), amplitude a -> 0 so c -> 1/2. The test reads tr(K^T K Omega) >= (1/2) <<K W^T + V K^T Gamma>>. Young: <dB, Psi dB> >= 2 <Xi, dB> - <<Xi>> with Xi = [0 | K W^T + V K^T Gamma]. <Xi, dB> = tr(K^T K Omega) + <Gamma, K N>, since K^T V = 0 and Gamma M_0^T = 0. Together: <dB, Psi dB> >= 2 <Gamma, K N>. (3) Take Pi_t the projector in whitened class space, orthogonal to 1 and to C_bar^(1/2) V', Pi_0t = J - V_t V_t^T, E_t their difference, R_t = Gamma_t + g_t sigma_t V_t Btil_t^T, Xi = -C_bar^(1/2) E_t R_t. Xi - Gamma = -C_bar^(1/2) Pi_t R_t, which V' annihilates. Gain: <V M_0, E... > becomes <V_t M_t, E_t R_t> = g_t sigma_t X_t. Cost: <<Xi>> <= |E_t R_t|_F^2 / ell <= 2 X_t g_t^2 / ell. (4) In whitened coordinates, K_t = u a^T, N_t = t a v^T: the ratio 2 t g_t / (|a^T M_t|^2 + t^2) has maximum g_t / sigma_t at t = sigma_t.

statements.statement: J2 (graded in defects). Let (A_0, V, M_0) be any triple, not nec. stationary, D_0 its loss, Gamma_0 = [Gamma_Y | Gamma], P_V = V V^T, P_M the projector on the row space of M_0, Q = (I - P_V) Gamma (I - P_M), Delta = Gamma_0 - [0 | Q], R = Q + w V Btil^T. For any competitor span Pi, if the Fisher point for Xi = Delta - [0 | E R] has g >= -a, then D(l') >= D_0 + w X - c(a) <<Xi>>, where <<Xi>> is the Psi^-1 form at the triple's own q. So, for any theta > 0: D_0 - L_Z(k) <= c(a) (1 + theta) <<Delta>> + sup over Pi of [c(a) (1 + 1/theta) <<E R>> - w X]_+ . At a stationary triple Delta = 0, and this is J1. If the second term vanishes (strict test), the bound is c(a) (1 + theta) <<Delta>>. Tightness: near a strict stationary triple, bound / true gap stays bounded as the defects tend to 0, since both are positive definite quadratic forms of Delta in finite dimension. Its limit depends on the triple.
statements.proof: Moment of q° - s: Xi - Gamma_0 = [0 | -E R - Q] = [0 | -Pi R], since Pi_0 R = Q (V^T Q = 0, 1^T Q = 0). This annihilates B' as in J1. H sum: -<B_0, Xi> = -<B_0, Delta> + <V M_0, E R>. <B_0, Delta> = <B_0, Gamma_0> because <B_0, [0|Q]> = tr(M_0^T V^T Q) = 0. <V M_0, E R> = tr(V^T E Q M_0^T) + w tr(Btil^T M_0^T V^T E V) = w X, using Q M_0^T = 0 and Btil^T M_0^T = I. D_0 = sum p (H(q) - H(s)) - <Gamma_0, B_0>. So D(l') >= D_0 + w X - sum p KL(q°||q), then part 2 of J1. Split with (u + v)^2 <= (1+theta) u^2 + (1 + 1/theta) v^2 in the Psi^-1 norm.

statements.statement: J3.1 (what z cannot compute: exact split). Let Z be any code space with basis zeta. The full-rank read least L_Z^inf = min over all B of D(B) is attained at B*, q* = softmax(B* zeta), because s > 0 makes D coercive. For every B': D(B') = L_Z^inf + sum p KL(q* || softmax(B' zeta)). So L_Z(k) = L_Z^inf + R_k(q*), R_k the rank-k read least of the table q*, and L_Z(k) >= L_Z^inf + L_free(k; q*). (Converse of TQ14 part 6.) With T empty, L_on(k) = L_free(k) exactly when some free-code least of s has logits in the read, because both infima are attained. (Fixed span.) If (t, V, c) is free-stationary with G V = 0, then for a read at the same span V: D - D(free) = sum p KL(q || softmax(t' + V M z)), exactly. L_Z^inf is a convex program, 0 exactly when log s_x is affine in zeta_x modulo 1, and it names no build, size or zoom.
statements.proof: TQ20 with sum p (s - q*) zeta^T = 0 gives the identity: the linear term vanishes for all B'. R_k >= L_free(k; q*) since reads are free codes. Attainment: the set of rank <= k matrices is closed and D is coercive modulo constants, for rows of free logits and for B alike. A read least with value L_free is then a free least in the read. Fixed span: TQ20, and sum p <s - q, V (c' - c)> = 0 by G V = 0 row by row.

statements.statement: J3.2 (class-mean read: exact cost identity and its small-noise value). T empty. Regions A_c, s_x = sbar_c on A_c. For a read B write l_x = B zeta_x, lbar_c its p-mean on A_c, qbar_c = softmax(lbar_c), K_q(d) = log E_q e^d - E_q d >= 0. (1) D(B) = T(B) + N(B), with T(B) = sum pi_c KL(sbar_c || qbar_c) >= L_table(k) and N(B) = sum over c, x in A_c of p_x K_(qbar_c)(l_x - lbar_c). So L_on(k) - L_table(k) = min over B of [T(B) - L_table(k) + N(B)]. (2) Let z_x = zbar_c + nu w_x, mean of w zero on each region, zbar_c affinely independent, and let the table least have finitely many minimiser logit tables. Then as nu -> 0+: L_on(k) = L_table(k) + nu^2 N_2 + o(nu^2), with N_2 = (1/2) min, over table minimisers (V, c*) and reads M with M zbar_c + beta = c*_c, of sum p_x Var_(q*_c)(V M w_x). (3) If the matrices V^T Cov(q*_c) V all equal Lambda and within-class covariances all equal Sigma with range holding the centred zbar: N_2 = (1/2) tr(Lambda C* (Zbar Sigma^+ Zbar^T)^+ C*^T), with Zbar and C* centred with pi-weights and the sum over pi-weighted Sigma. Read through canonical correlations rho_j of z with the region at small nu: the cost is a sum of (1 - rho_j^2)/rho_j^2 times the Fisher-weighted code energy on direction j. Warning from F8: the formula is in spans. A direction of tiny variance is usable with weights of size 1/e.
statements.proof: (1) A(l_x) = A(lbar_c) + <qbar_c, l_x - lbar_c> + K_(qbar_c)(l_x - lbar_c), and E <sbar_c, l_x> = <sbar_c, lbar_c>. Average over the region; the linear term has mean 0. lbar_c = t + V M zbar_c has rank k. (2) Upper: take a minimiser and the least M; K_q(d) = (1/2) Var_q(d) + O(|d|^3). Lower: let B_nu be least; then D(B_nu) <= L_table + O(nu^2), so T(B_nu) -> L_table, so lbar_c tends to a minimiser, so qbar_c >= q_0 > 0. K_q(d) >= Var_q(d) / (2 + osc d), from Var_(q_t)(d) >= e^(-t osc) Var_q(d). N = O(nu^2) then forces osc(l_x - lbar_c) = O(nu), so V M_nu w is bounded, and M_nu tends along a subsequence to a read that writes the minimiser. Its noise is >= 2 N_2 / 2. (3) Quadratic program with Lagrange multipliers. The canonical form is a reading of (3), since within whitening Sigma_B + nu^2 Sigma = I; I state it as a reading, not as a separate theorem.

statements.statement: J3.3 (exact read cost at a binding rank, at any confidence). K = C = 2k >= 4, pi_c = 1/K, sbar_c = a on class c and b on each other class, a > b > 0, r = a - b. Each region A_c has rows x with z_x = y_x e_c in R^K and y_x >= 0. The p-law of y on A_c is the same for all c, E y = 1, y not a.s. 0 (normalisation), and Z = the span of 1 and the K coordinates of z. So z has within-class variation, and D may be K + 1 > k. Let tau be the unique root of E[ y (u^y - u^-y) / (u^y + u^-y + K - 2) ] = r, with u = e^tau. Then L_on(k) = L_Z(k) = E log(2 cosh(tau y) + K - 2) - r tau - H(sbar). The pole read attains it: l_x = tau y_x (e_c - e_c'), for any pairing. L_free(k) = L_table(k) is the same formula at y = 1 (TQ17 part 4). So L_on(k) > L_free(k) unless y is a.s. constant, and the cost is exact.
statements.proof: Upper side. q_x has u_x/Z_x on c, 1/(u_x Z_x) on c', 1/Z_x elsewhere, with u_x = e^(tau y_x). Write qq, q', q'' for these. D = E[H(q_x)] - H(sbar) + sum p <q_x - s_x, log q_x>, and with kappa_x = r - (qq - q'), s_c - q_x = a_x Pi* e_c + (kappa_x/2)(e_c - e_c'), a_x = K (q'' - b). Pi* kills e_c - e_c', so the last sum is -tau E[kappa y] = 0 at the root. E[H(q_x)] = E log Z - tau E[y (qq - q')] = E log Z - tau r. Lower side. Fix a competitor l'_x = t' + y_x B'_c with B'_c = V' M' e_c. Let Pi be a rank k - 1 projector with Pi 1 = 0, V'^T Pi = 0, E = Pi - Pi*, and alpha_x = 2 (q'' - q') >= 0. Define q°_x = q_x - alpha_x E e_c. Key identity: E[alpha y] = E[a_x y]. Proof: with A = E[qq y], A' = E[q' y], A'' = E[q'' y], we have A - A' = r and A + A' + (K-2) A'' = 1, so 2 (A'' - A') = K A'' - (1 - r) = K (A'' - b). Positivity as in TQ17: on diagonal and tails, E_ci <= 1/2 and alpha/2 <= q'' - q', so the entry is >= q' > 0; at the partner the entry is q' + alpha T. Feasibility: q° - s = (alpha_x - a_x) Pi* e_c - alpha_x Pi e_c - (kappa_x/2)(e_c - e_c'). Against t': each part sums to 0 over c, since the law of y is common. Against y B'_c: E[(alpha - a) y] = 0, Pi B'_c = 0, E[kappa y] = 0. So D(l') >= sum p (H(q°) - H(sbar)). Expand by (E) of TQ17: row bracket = alpha_x tau y_x (D_c + T_c) - sum q phi(-alpha_x E / q). Sum over c of E[alpha tau y] D_c = 0, since tr Pi = k - 1 = K beta. The row identity (R) and the entry bounds give the bracket >= g_x(T_c) with g_x(T) = (alpha tau_x - gamma_x) T + gamma_x T^2 - q' phi(alpha T / q'), tau_x = tau y_x, gamma_x = 4 q'' phi(-alpha / (2 q'')). This g_x has exactly the form of TQ17 part 4 at u = u_x: g''' > 0, g(0) = g(1/2) = g'(1/2) = 0, so g_x >= 0 on [0,1]. At y_x = 0, alpha = 0 and g_x = 0. So D(l') >= E H(q_x) - H(sbar). Strictness: x -> log(2 cosh x + K - 2) is strictly convex and E y = 1, so E Phi(tau y) > Phi(tau) for each tau != 0 when y is not a.s. constant. The root is unique, by strict convexity of D in tau, with derivative -r at 0 and 1 - r at infinity.

statements.statement: J3.4 (the confident read cost is much larger than the rank cost). In J3.3, m = log(a/b), e = 1 - a = (K - 1) b, y_min the least value of y, with y_min > 0, p_0 = P(y = y_min), rho_0 = K b / (p_0 y_min) < 1. Then H(sbar) = (K-1) b m - log a, and b m (K/y_min - K + 1) + (K b / y_min) log((K-2)(1-rho_0) p_0 y_min / K) + log a <= L_on(k) <= b m (K/y_min - K + 1) + e^2 / a. So at fixed K and law, L_on(k) = b m (K/y_min - K + 1) + O(b), and L_free(k) = b m + O(b). As m -> infinity, L_on(k) / L_free(k) -> 1 + K (1/y_min - 1). The read cost is about e m (1/y_min - 1) at K large: it depends on the worst row of a class, and it charges all tail classes. If p_0 is below K b / y_min, the worst rows may misrank instead. The value is then given by the exact one-variable formula of J3.3, in the manner of a tail quantile of y at level about K b.
statements.proof: With log(2 cosh x + K-2) = x + log(1 + (K-2) e^-x + e^-2x), E y = 1, r = 1 - K b: D(tau) = K b tau + E log(1 + (K-2) e^(-tau y) + e^(-2 tau y)) - (K-1) b m + log a. Upper: tau = m / y_min gives e^(-tau y) <= b/a, so the log term is <= (K-1) b/a. And log a <= -(K-1) b. The sum is (K-1) b (1/a - 1) = e^2 / a. Lower: for every tau >= 0 the log term is >= p_0 log(1 + (K-2) e^(-tau y_min)). The minimum over tau of K b tau + that term is at psi/(1+psi) = rho_0, psi = (K-2) e^(-tau y_min), and it is >= K b tau*, with tau* y_min = log((K-2)(1-rho_0)/rho_0) = -log b + log((K-2)(1-rho_0) p_0 y_min / K) >= m + log(...), since -log b = m - log a >= m.
