statements.statement: J4.1 (hinge form of a gate; the read is generically not V_b). (1) Every gated build is a read plus hinges: l' = l'' + sum over j of v_j (-u_j)_+, with l'' = t' + A h_T + sum v_j u_j, u_j = m_j . z + beta_j. In code form: with c = M z, y = R c in any basis R, the code is max(y, theta) coordinate by coordinate. (2) Let l be any always-on build with codes c_x, r_x = s_x - q_x, x_0 a row with unique code at a vertex of conv{c_x}, a in the open normal cone with gap gamma = the next least of a . c_x above a . c_(x_0), and a . b = 1. For delta in (0, gamma]: the build l + V b (a . c_(x_0) + delta - a . c)_+ has k units, and D falls by p_(x_0) [KL(s_(x_0)||q_(x_0)) - KL(s_(x_0)||softmax(l_(x_0) + delta V b))], with first-order slope p_(x_0) <r_(x_0), V b>. (3) So if L_on(k) = V_b(k) with a least triple: at k >= 2, V^T r_x = 0 at each such vertex row (for rows that share a vertex code, the p-weighted sum is 0). At k = 1 with unit vector v of V: <r, v> <= 0 at the lowest row of the code and >= 0 at the highest row. With stationarity sum p <r,v> = 0 and sum p <r,v> c = 0, that needs at least 3 sign changes of <r,v> along the code. A saturating target has the wrong pattern. (4) This is a limit result on all L_on-based theorems at k >= 2: a certificate of L_on (E6, J1) gives V(G) only with this vertex condition or the free-code test of TQ18.1. A limit result fills no slot.
statements.proof: (1) relu(u) = u + (-u)_+. Basis: V M = (V R^-1)(R M), and R can have a as a row with b the matching column of R^-1 exactly when a . b = 1. (2) Only x_0 is below the kink for delta <= gamma. Use the unit with row a, moved down by its bias so that the kink is at a . c_(x_0) + delta. The others stay on by large bias. (3) If V^T r_bar != 0 at k >= 2, the open cone holds an a that is not a negative multiple of V^T r_bar, and then some b has a . b = 1 and <V^T r_bar, b> > 0. So D falls. At k = 1, a and b have one sign: bottom row a > 0, b > 0; top row a < 0, b < 0. The sign count: a function orthogonal to the affine functions of c has at least 2 sign changes; the ends fix an odd number.

statements.statement: J4.2 (a gate can remove all of the read cost; a jump). On the family of J3.3 with y_x > 0 on all rows: V_b(k) = L_free(k) = L_table(k) < L_on(k), unless y is a.s. constant. So L_on(k) - V_b(k) is the full closed-form cost of J3.3, and by J3.4 L_on / V_b -> 1 + K (1/y_min - 1) at confidence. The build uses read weights of size 1/y_min. Jump: for every y_min > 0 the value V_b(k) = L_table(k) does not depend on y_min. If instead a mass p_0 of rows per region has y_x = 0, then V_b(k) >= p_0 (log K - H(sbar)). So V_b jumps as y_min -> 0+, while L_on's formula is continuous there. So no bound on V_b in a distance on z can be continuous, in the manner of F8. Random-start fits are not evidence: the gated optimum needs off rows and the fits below can miss it.
statements.proof: Take H an invertible k x k matrix of +-1, columns h_j (H = 1 1^T - 2 I for k >= 3; [[1,1],[1,-1]] at k = 2), G = H^-1. On regions of pair j let the bit vectors be w = (1 + h_j)/2 at c, w = (1 - h_j)/2 at c'. Then pole code = tau G (2 w - 1): plus or minus tau e_j. So the pole logits equal t' + V' w, with V' = 2 tau V_pole G and t' = -tau V_pole G 1. Unit i: u_i = 1 - L times the sum of z[c] over classes c with w_c[i] = 0, with L >= 1/y_min. On a region with w[i] = 1, u_i = 1, because z[c''] = 0 for the other classes and the coefficient of its own class is 0. On a region with w[i] = 0, u_i = 1 - L y_x <= 0. So relu(u_i) = w_c[i] exactly on every row. Loss = L_table(k) at tau_0. With TQ11 part 1 and TQ14 part 4, V_b(k) = L_free(k) = L_table(k). Jump: rows with y = 0 all have z = 0, so one code and one q_0, and the mean of KL(sbar_c||q_0) over c is at least log K - H(sbar), the Jensen gap at mean uniform.

statements.statement: J4.3 (indicator and separation claims: gate-aware claims on N). Let B be a set of rows and S a group. Indicator claim error: eps_ind(S, B) = min over m, beta of the sum over x in B of p_x (m . z_x + beta - 1)^2 plus the sum over x not in B of p_x (m . z_x + beta)_+^2. Separation claim error: eps_sep(S, B) = min over m, beta of the sum over B of p_x (1 - m . z_x - beta)_+^2 plus the sum outside B of p_x (m . z_x + beta)_+^2. Both are convex and polynomial. eps_ind = 0 exactly when some unit relu(m . z + beta) equals 1_B at every row with p > 0. eps_sep = 0 exactly when z_S separates B from its complement with a margin. Neither names a build, target size or zoom. Both are unchanged by copies and by rescaling of units, because m is free. (1) Exact: T empty, constancy claim error 0. Suppose the table least at k is attained by (t, V, c) with region codes c_r = alpha(w_r), alpha affine, w_r in {0,1}^k, and the k claims eps_ind(S, B_j) = 0 hold with B_j = the union of regions where w_r[j] = 1. Then V_b(k) = L_free(k) = L_table(k), for z that may vary inside regions. This covers TQ17's pole family (cross-polytope = affine image of antipodal bits, as in J4.2) and TQ21's table (k = 2^m - 1, one-hot on 2^m families). (2) Two-sided clip: if eps_sep(S, B_j) = 0 for j = 1..k', then V_b(2 k') <= L_bin(k') := min over t, V of the sum of p KL(s_x || softmax(t + V w_x)), with w_x the bit vector, and L_free(2 k') <= V_b(2 k'). So at twice the width, gates write a noise-free binary code under dense bounded variation. (3) Graded, for the build only: if units are taken from eps_ind's optimum, then sum p |relu(u_j) - 1_(B_j)|^2 <= eps_ind(S, B_j). If in addition G V = 0 at the ideal build (true on TQ17's family), the build's loss minus L_table is exactly sum p K_(q_x)(V e_x), with e_x the code error. That is at most (1/2) e^omega sum p Var_(q_x)(V e_x), omega = the largest osc(V e_x). It depends on V, so on tau, so it is not a bound in the errors alone. It bounds the build, not V_b - L_table from both sides.
statements.proof: Zero sets: eps_ind = 0 forces u = 1 on B and u <= 0 off B. eps_sep = 0 forces u >= 1 on B and u <= 0 off B. (1) Rows: relu(u_j) = w_r[j]. Then t + V c_r = t + V alpha(w_r), an affine image: a k-unit build with the same logits, with loss L_table(k). TQ11 part 1 and TQ14 part 4 give the lower side. (2) clip = relu(u) - relu(u - 1) equals 1_B on all rows, using out-weights +v, -v, so 2 units per bit and logit rank k'. (3) On B, (relu(u) - 1)^2 <= (u - 1)^2: for u < 0 the left is 1 and the right is above 1. Off B equal. TQ20 at G V = 0 gives the exact K form. K_q(d) <= Var_q(d) e^(osc d) / 2, since e^y - 1 - y <= (y^2/2) e^(|y|).

statements.statement: J4.4 (lower bounds on V_b that use gates). (1) Trim: for a gated build let O_j be the off set of unit j and S the union of the O_j. Then D >= the least of the read at rank k on rows P \ S, with weights p unnormalised. So V_b(k) >= min over unions S of k half-spaces of L_Z^(P\S)(k), and a build with p(S) <= mu is at least that min over p(S) <= mu. (2) Cuts: for a tuple of half-space cuts S_1..S_k, all code columns lie in Z^(S) = the span of 1 and of 1_(not S_j) times (1, z), for j = 1..k. So V_b(k) >= min over cut tuples of L_(Z^(S))(k), and J1 applies to each cut tuple. The number of tuples is polynomial in n at fixed D and k, and it is not modest at D = 512.
statements.proof: (1) On P \ S all units are on, so l' is a rank-k read there, and KL >= 0 on S. (2) relu(u_j) = u_j 1_(not S_j), and a rank-k code class on a space contains it. L_Z is defined for any space that holds 1.

statements.statement: J4.5 (a proved condition for the always-on read to be least among gated boxes, k = 1). T empty, distinct codes on P as needed below. Let s_0 = softmax(t_0 + v* f_0), J v* != 0, f_0 = m* . z + beta*, with a unique lowest row x_- and a unique highest row x_+ of f_0. Rows other than x_- affinely span the z-space, and likewise rows other than x_+. 1_(x_-) and 1_(x_+) are outside Z. Let s_eps = softmax(l_0 + eps h). Let T = {tau + w f_0 + v* g: tau, w in R^C, g in Z}, let h° be the Fisher projection of h on T at q_0, and rho_x = Cov(q_0,x)(h_x - h°_x). If <rho_(x_-), v*> < 0 and <rho_(x_+), v*> > 0, then there is eps_0 > 0 with V_b(1) = L_on(1) for 0 < eps < eps_0. If either sign is reversed, then V_b(1) < L_on(1) for small eps, by J4.1. Under the premise L_free(1) < L_on(1) for small eps. So this is a case with L_free < V_b = L_on, on a table whose loss is of order eps^2. It is perturbative, and it stops at finite eps: a finite interior cut can win even when the ends have the right sign. For k >= 2 no analogue holds without the vertex condition of J4.1. For C = 2, k = 1 there is also an exact finite test: V_b(1) is the least of 4(n - 1) convex programs with the sign constraints kept, for a scalar read.
statements.proof: V_b(1) <= L_on(1) by TQ11. Let gated builds t_n + v_n relu(u_n) have loss below L_on(1; eps_n) with eps_n -> 0. Loss -> 0 and s_eps -> s_0 > 0, so logits tend to l_0 modulo constants on each row. Scale so that J v_n -> sigma J v*, sigma = +-1. Then sigma (h_n(x) - h_n(y)) -> f_0(x) - f_0(y), with h_n = relu(u_n) >= 0. So h_n = sigma f_0 + a_n + o(1), and off rows all share one value of sigma f_0, which must be its minimum: for large n the off set is empty or {x_-} (sigma = +1) or {x_+} (sigma = -1). If it is empty, the build is a read, and its loss is >= L_on(1). Otherwise take sigma = +1. All other rows are on, so u_n is affine there and tends to f_0 + a by the span premise, and u_n -> 0 at x_-. So l^n = read + kappa v_n 1_(x_-), kappa >= 0 small. Near Theta_0 = (t_0, v*, m*, beta*, kappa = 0) modulo gauge, the problem is smooth with one constraint kappa >= 0. At eps = 0, l_0 is the unique minimiser with positive definite Fisher Hessian, because v* 1_(x_-) is outside T: if it were in T, then v* (a function in Z) + w f_0 + tau would equal it, and applying J and a direction across v* forces 1_(x_-) in Z. The second-order model is the Fisher projection of h on T plus a cone in v* 1_(x_-). Its multiplier at kappa = 0 is -p <rho_(x_-), v*> > 0, so strict complementarity holds, and by the implicit function theorem the exact minimiser for small eps has kappa = 0. So no gated build in the neighbourhood beats the read, a contradiction. Sign reversed: J4.1 part 2 at the row x_-, with a first-order residual proportional to rho. L_free: free codes project out v* row by row, so their second-order model removes <rho_x, v*> at all rows, including x_-, which is nonzero.

statements.statement: Three failures, each with its step. (a) Removing positivity from J1. Target: a uniform bound on the exact exponential dual's cost B(Xi), for all spans, without g >= -a. I proved only B(Xi) <= 2 (1 - sqrt(1 - xi U))^2 / U^2 for xi U < 1, with xi^2 = <<Xi>> and U = the sup of osc(F zeta_x) over <F, Psi F> = 1. That is the same cap as E6's second condition. (b) A linear-probability dual for L_Z^inf: q° = s + theta (P s - s), P the p-projection on Z. It is feasible and closed form, but on the pole read at D = k it is vacuous at confidence, because a read of k dimensions cannot fit K classes linearly, though it fits them exponentially, so the cost of lifting tails exceeds the gain.
